title: Ed Sheeran music dropped by Irish radio station after Palestine row
author: Our Foreign Staff
content:
![Ed Sheeran (left) and Macklemore, the rapper, perform on stage at the 2014 iHeartRadio Music Festival at the MGM Grand Garden Arena on Sept 20, 2014 in Las Vegas, Nevada](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/world-news/2026/09/17/TELEMMGLPICT000503310534_17896352065390_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqBqQpMmcJbyOsM10vwHMrJha306WnPHVE_UdBq2uCdwc.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Ed Sheeran (left) and Macklemore, the rapper, perform on stage at the 2014 iHeartRadio Music Festival at the MGM Grand Garden Arena on Sept 20, 2014 in Las Vegas, Nevada](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/world-news/2026/09/17/TELEMMGLPICT000503310534_17896352065390_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqBqQpMmcJbyOsM10vwHMrJha306WnPHVE_UdBq2uCdwc.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
An Irish radio station has dropped Ed Sheeran’s music after listeners complained about the Palestine row surrounding his US tour.
Listeners called for a boycott after Macklemore, one of Sheeran’s support acts, was removed from the tour over his pro-Palestinian views.
During a show at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, Macklemore had said he wanted people in Gaza and the West Bank to know they had not been forgotten.
After he was removed from the tour, all the other support acts on Sheeran’s Loop tour dropped out of the remaining dates.
Classic Hits Radio, based in Ireland, said it had decided to remove Sheeran’s music for the “foreseeable future” after listener feedback.
![Ed Sheeran with Macklemore](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/world-news/2026/09/17/TELEMMGLPICT000503309514_17896352063992_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqKU-op6n8Xxa2ymKjnWOvoQpXsRmTSpNSq5uXjoPr_PU.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Dave Kelly, the group programme director at Bay Broadcasting, which runs the station, said: “Our decision to remove Ed Sheeran’s music from the Classic Hits Radio playlist has been carefully considered.
“As an independent Irish-owned radio station, we believe it is important to listen to our audience and to stand alongside Irish artists who have made what is undoubtedly a significant professional decision based on their own convictions.
“In light of the strength of feeling expressed by our listeners, and the decisions taken by Irish artists involved in the tour, we believe removing Ed Sheeran’s music from our playlist is the appropriate decision for Classic Hits Radio at this time.”
Aaron Rowe, an Irish singer, Finneas, who is Billie Eilish’s brother, and Lukas Graham, a Danish singer, as well as Beoga, Sheeran’s backing band, shared messages of support for Macklemore after also withdrawing from the tour.
The rapper has donated his $1m (£747,328) net earnings from the tour to charities supporting Palestinian people, and has challenged Robert Kraft, the billionaire owner of the Gillette Stadium who called for his removal from the tour, to match his donation.
He wrote on Instagram: “With everything that has happened over the last 48 hours, I want to bring the conversation back to where it belongs: to the Palestinian people who are still being killed, still living under military occupation and still fighting for their freedom.
“I will be donating the entire one million of my net earnings from Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour to six organisations working directly to support the Palestinian people.”
![Macklemore challenged Robert Kraft to match his donation](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/world-news/2026/09/17/TELEMMGLPICT000500143239_17896350192490_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqTeEWZJutNXs-DTiHB68zoCzX6hXnrjGR-O-DrJVhEdw.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Addressing Mr Kraft, he added that “whatever we disagree about, perhaps we can agree on this, Palestinian lives are worth protecting, a Palestinian life is no less valuable than any other life on this Earth”.
Mr Kraft, a Jewish-American businessman, wrote in a statement on Instagram: “I have dedicated much of my life to building bridges between all people. I believe deeply that all lives are worth protecting.
“Earlier today, before Macklemore challenged me to match his donation, Ed called me and asked me to commit two million to match his donation to aid in the region to fight this humanitarian crisis.
“Ed now plans to reach out to other venue owners, and our goal is to continue to work together to build bridges.
“In addition, I’d like the people who are speaking in support of the Palestinian people to know that for decades, I have supported efforts that create opportunity for Palestinians and have brought young Palestinians and Israelis together to build businesses, create jobs and forge relationships.”
![Robert Kraft, pictured with his wife Dana Blumberg, says he has been bringing Palestinians and Israelis together for decades](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/briefs/2026/09/16/TELEMMGLPICT000503291331_17895651088203_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqkjTqN4q_QOMdsQB6negVQk8FchWZRD3tSYOiRwPjWDo.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
On Tuesday, Sheeran said on social media that Macklemore’s departure from the tour was the promoter’s decision and not his, after a petition was launched to get the rapper removed.
He said “upcoming tour dates had communicated that they would pull the shows if he was still supporting”, and added that Mr Kraft, whose Gillette Stadium will host gigs on Oasis’s Live 27 tour, was among them.
Sheeran, 35, insisted that he was “not complicit”, that he has his “personal views on this devastating conflict” and was “appalled by the conflict between Israel and Palestine”. He added that he respected Macklemore “as an artist”.
In a previous statement shared by Mr Kraft, the businessman said his decision to ban the US rapper following his comments on stage were down to a “broader history of anti-Semitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community”.
Sheeran’s next performance is scheduled to take place on Sept 19 at the Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, where Graham and Rowe had been scheduled to open for him.
He has 17 dates left on the tour, which spans North and South America, with the final show scheduled for Dec 11 in Mexico City.
summary: Irish radio station Classic Hits Radio has dropped Ed Sheeran's music for the foreseeable future following listener complaints regarding a Palestine row on his US tour. The controversy began when rapper Macklemore was removed as a support act over pro-Palestinian views, prompting other artists and backing band members to also withdraw from remaining dates. Sheeran stated that Macklemore's removal was decided by promoters due to threats of canceled shows from venue owners, including Robert Kraft.
key_points: Classic Hits Radio in Ireland removed Ed Sheeran's music from its playlist following listener feedback.
Rapper Macklemore was removed from Sheeran's US tour after expressing pro-Palestinian views on stage.
Following Macklemore's removal, other support acts and Sheeran's backing band withdrew from the remaining tour dates in support of the rapper.
Macklemore donated his $1 million net tour earnings to charities supporting Palestinian people and challenged Robert Kraft to match the donation.
Ed Sheeran stated that Macklemore's departure was the promoter's decision rather than his own, and insisted he is appalled by the conflict.

title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day just thwipped past Star Wars to reach an all-time box office record
author: Jordan King
summary: Spider-Man: Brand New Day has broken the all-time US box office record, grossing $936.7 million stateside 47 days after its release. Directed by Destin Daniel Cretton and starring Tom Holland and Zendaya, the film has also reached $2.45 billion globally to become the third highest-grossing film ever. Lucasfilm paid tribute to the movie's record-breaking success on Instagram following its surpass of Star Wars.
key_points: Spider-Man: Brand New Day is now the highest-grossing movie ever at the US box office with $936.7 million.
The film has reached a global total of $2.45 billion, making it the third highest-grossing film worldwide.
Lucasfilm acknowledged the film's domestic record-breaking milestone with an Instagram post.
The movie's success contributes to Hollywood's biggest box office summer and a record-breaking year for the industry.

title: Robert Kraft says Ed Sheeran asked him to donate $2m to aid after Macklemore backlash
author: Nardine Saad
content:
Will Ed Sheeran cancel his tour as support acts quit?
- Published
Robert Kraft, the US stadium owner who had pro-Palestinian rapper Macklemore removed as Ed Sheeran's opening act at his venue, says Sheeran has asked him to match a $2m (Â£1.5m) donation to "aid in the region".
The request came after Macklemore separately said he would donate $1m (Â£750,000) to Palestinian organisations, challenging Kraft to match the sum.
Kraft, the owner of the New England Patriots, wrote on Wednesday: "Earlier today, before Macklemore challenged me to match his donation, Ed called me and asked me to commit $2 million to match his donation to aid in the region to fight this humanitarian crisis.
"Ed now plans to reach out to other venue owners and our goal is to continue to work together to build bridges."
Kraft did not confirm whether he has agreed to make the $2m donation or where the funds will go, and Sheeran himself has not commented about any donation he is making or other philanthropic plans.
Kraft's comments came in his second statement this week on the controversy over Sheeran's US tour.
On Monday, he confirmed he had Macklemore dropped as the opening act from the bill for British singer's forthcoming performance at his Gillette Stadium near Boston, accusing the rapper of hate speech during a previous show for calling for "Free Palestine" and making other comments and showing images of Gaza on stage.
Macklemore's removal sparked a backlash, with Sheeran's other support acts dropping out in protest.
Sheeran has said the decision to drop Macklemore from his Loop Tour was made by promoters and that he would not be drawn into a public debate over Gaza.
![New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft wears a Patriots hat and looks on during Super Bowl LX Opening Night at San Jose McEnery Convention Center on 2 February 2026 in San Jose, California.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/8792/live/5f0fd970-b22e-11f1-8366-69bd8e92a4f2.jpg)
US billionaire Robert Kraft
In the statement, which was issued by Gillette Stadium on Kraft's behalf, he said he would like those speaking in support of the Palestinian people to know that he has long "supported efforts that create opportunity for Palestinians".
He also said that he has worked to bring "young Palestinians and Israelis together to build businesses, create jobs, and forge relationships".
"I have dedicated much of my life to building bridges between all people," Kraft said. "I believe deeply that all lives are worth protecting."
The owner of the Kraft Group, a sports and event management company, did not say whether he had rallied other stadium owners to ban Macklemore from their venues, as the rapper claims.
Macklemore - real name Benjamin Haggerty - called for a "free Palestine" and showed images of devastation in Gaza during two Sheeran concerts in New Jersey earlier this month.
He was dropped on Monday from Sheeran's line-up, just days before the tour was set to resume in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, on Saturday.
Sheeran, who performed at Kraft's 2022 wedding, said on Tuesday he was not responsible for Macklemore being removed as an opening act from the tour.
Kraft, who is Jewish, confirmed on Monday that he had made the decision to bar Macklemore from the Gillette Stadium because his venue would not "provide a platform for hate speech".
The tycoon accused the Grammy-winning rapper of having "a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric", which Macklemore denies.
He also said the pro-Palestinian artist was "only sharing selective information and ignoring the actions of Hamas".
All the other support acts from Sheeran's US tour have since quit in solidarity with Macklemore.
They are Finneas, the brother of pop star Billie Eilish, Irish singer-songwriter Aaron Rowe and Danish band Lukas Graham, as well as Irish folk band Beoga, who perform with Sheeran on stage every night.
The artists argued that Macklemore's removal represented a chilling effect on free speech.
Macklemore said on Wednesday he would donate the entire $1m of his net earnings from Sheeran's Loop Tour to six Palestinian organisations "to bring the conversation back to where it belongs: to the Palestinian people".
"This is a manmade injustice, and I believe it requires immediate political change," he wrote on social media.

On the right, there is a graphic of an orange sphere with two concentric crescent shapes around it in a red-orange gradient, like a sound wave. The banner reads: âThe latest news in your inbox first thing.â](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/7aee/live/b9fd0f10-b260-11f1-a430-4d16ee157c41.png)
summary: US stadium owner Robert Kraft stated that Ed Sheeran asked him to match a $2m donation to aid the humanitarian crisis in the region following controversy over the removal of rapper Macklemore from Sheeran's tour. Macklemore, who was dropped by Kraft for his pro-Palestinian remarks at a previous concert, separately challenged Kraft to match his own $1m donation to Palestinian organisations. The backlash over Macklemore's removal has led all other support acts on Sheeran's US tour to drop out in protest.
key_points: Robert Kraft stated that Ed Sheeran asked him to commit $2m to aid in the region.
Macklemore challenged Kraft to match his $1m donation to Palestinian organisations.
Kraft previously had Macklemore removed from the Gillette Stadium lineup over pro-Palestinian comments, which Kraft labeled hate speech.
All other support acts for Sheeran's US tour have quit in protest of Macklemore's removal.

title: Box Office: ‘Resident Evil’ Reboot Targets Franchise-Best $45 Million Debut
author: Rebecca Rubin
content:
Movie theater operators are counting on “Resident Evil” to scare some life into the early fall box office.
Sony’s horror-comedy reboot of the zombie-infested property is targeting a strong $40 million to $50 million in its domestic debut. With strong reviews and glowing word-of-mouth, rivals and independent tracking services believe that initial ticket sales will surpass $50 million and could near $60 million.
Sony spent $75 million to produce the movie, the second remake and eighth installment in the horror series. Exhibitors are particularly excited because this take on “Resident Evil” was directed by Zach Cregger, who electrified the box office with last August’s breakout hit “Weapons.” That R-rated movie, an original thriller about students who went missing in the middle of the night, opened to $43 million en route to sleeper hit status. “Weapons” ended its box office run with a mighty $270 million globally against a $38 million budget and won an Oscar for Amy Madigan.
Popular on Variety
“Resident Evil” began as a 1996 video game and expanded into a multimedia franchise that spans sequel games and film and television adaptations. The property was first adapted for the big screen in 2002’s “Resident Evil,” starring Milla Jovovich. She reprised her role as Alice, a former security specialist and covert operative, in five follow-up films in the 2000s and 2010s. Those movies collectively generated $1 billion globally and were once the highest-grossing series based on video games. Sony attempted to reboot the property with 2021’s “Resident Evil: Welcome to Raccoon City,” a critical and commercial failure with $42 million worldwide against a $25 million budget. All of the original “Resident Evil” films opened in the $20 million range (not adjusted for inflation), while “Welcome to Raccoon City” faltered with $5.3 million in its debut, so this reboot will easily rank as the largest opening weekend in the long-running franchise. The highest grossing installment is 2010’s “Resident Evil: Afterlife,” which launched to $26 million domestically and ended its theatrical run with $300 million globally.
In the new “Resident Evil,” Cregger reunites with “Weapons” actor Austin Abrams, who stars as a medical courier who fights through a viral outbreak of infested monsters in Raccoon City. Critics have praised the cinematic gorefest, with Variety’s Owen Gleiberman calling it “different, and much better, than the other ‘Resident Evil’ movies.”
As this weekend’s only major release, “Resident Evil” won’t have any trouble securing the No. 1 spot on domestic box office charts. Elsewhere, “Practical Magic 2” will attempt to rebound after a rough start while mid-summer holdovers like “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and “The Odyssey” will remain atop box office charts.
Although this weekend is light on newcomers, the fall box office is expected to heat up before September ends. Next weekend brings a trio of new movies, including Paramount’s Brad Pitt-led survival thriller “Heart of the Beast,” Universal and DreamWorks Animation’s “Forgotten Island” and A24’s “To Catch a Predator”-inspired “Primetime,” starring Robert Pattinson. There’s also Disney’s re-release of “Avengers: Endgame,” which is returning to theaters before “Avengers: Doomsday” opens in December. In the meantime, it’s Cregger and his band of zombie slayers to the rescue.
summary: Sony's horror-comedy reboot of "Resident Evil" is projected to open domestically with $40 million to $50 million, with some tracking services suggesting it could surpass $60 million. Directed by Zach Cregger and starring Austin Abrams, the film cost $75 million to produce and is expected to achieve the largest opening weekend in the franchise's history. It will easily secure the No. 1 spot at the domestic box office as the weekend's only major release.
key_points: Sony's "Resident Evil" reboot is targeting a domestic debut between $40 million and $50 million.
The film was directed by Zach Cregger and produced for $75 million.
It reunites Cregger with "Weapons" actor Austin Abrams, who stars as a medical courier.
The movie will easily claim the No. 1 spot as this weekend's only major release.

title: Macklemore pledges his $1m Ed Sheeran tour salary to Palestine
author: Adrian Horton
content:
Macklemore has announced he will donate the $1m salary he was paid as an opening act for Ed Sheeran’s Loop tour to organizations working with Palestinian people and relief in Gaza, after being dropped from the tour following backlash to his onstage comments in support of Palestine.
The rapper also challenged Robert Kraft, the billionaire owner of the New England Patriots and prominent Israel donor who refused to let Macklemore play at his Gillette Stadium outside Boston, to match his donation.
“With everything that has happened over the last 48 hours, I want to bring the conversation back to where it belongs: to the Palestinian people who are still being killed, still living under military occupation, and still fighting for their freedom,” the Grammy-winning artist wrote on Instagram.
“I will be donating the entire $1 million of my net earnings from Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour to six organizations working directly to support the Palestinian people. And I invite Robert Kraft to match my donation. Whatever we disagree about, perhaps we can agree on this: Palestinian lives are worth protecting. A Palestinian life is no less valuable than any other life on this earth.”
In a two-minute speech during his set at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey earlier this month, Macklemore expressed his desire to see a “free Palestine. I want those words to be loud and clear, so that people all the way in Gaza to the occupied West Bank know that we have not forgotten about them.” His remarks prompted a petition from the Israeli-American Council demanding his removal from the tour.
Speaking again on stage the following day, he reiterated his support for Palestine and addressed Jewish members of the audience: “Criticism of Israel, criticism of apartheid, being against genocide in no way is a criticism of you. My message is for peace, love; for all human beings to be treated with dignity, respect and equality.”
According to Sheeran, who posted his own explanation on Tuesday morning outlining his desire to remain publicly neutral on political causes, Kraft, along with several other venue owners, informed the English singer that his tour could not play at their stadiums if Macklemore continued as an opener, prompting his removal. A day later, all four of Sheeran’s opening acts for the remainder of the Loop tour – Finneas, Aaron Rowe, Boega and Lukas Graham – withdrew from the tour in solidarity with Macklemore and Palestine.
In his post, Macklemore said he hoped to “center the parents carrying their children into hospitals without the basic resources to treat them, and the physicians, paramedics, journalists and aid workers who keep going back in. I want to center the organizers and activists who have paid real costs for standing with Palestine. Their risk is of a far different order than mine.”
He added: “Palestinians have lived for decades without basic rights and should not have to wait another day to be free. That is where my focus will remain. I will continue to stand with the Palestinian people and their fight for liberation. When the news cycle moves on, which it will, don’t move with it. Free Palestine.”
Earlier Wednesday, Colin Kaepernick, whose NFL career was effectively ended by the NFL’s resistance to his protests against US police violence, joined the chorus of prominent figures criticizing Macklemore’s removal at the behest of NFL stadium owners. “The part that I hope people appreciate and take away in this moment is what [New England Patriots owner] Robert Kraft and what they’re saying by denying Macklemore the opportunity to go out and perform with Ed Sheeran is they are willing to collude,” the former quarterback said on the MeidasTouch podcast. “The [NFL owners] are openly colluding.”
Kaepernick added that he thought NFL owners tried to hound out Macklemore in a similar way to him. “When we filed the grievance, it was like, well, the owners wouldn’t do that,” Kaepernick said. “Everybody just wants to win within the NFL. And the realization is, no. They want to protect their interests. They want to protect their power. They want to protect their money.”
In his own Monday statement, Kraft said his decision to ban Macklemore from the Patriots’ stadium was due to his “recent actions” and “a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community”.
summary: Rapper Macklemore announced he is donating his $1 million salary from Ed Sheeran's tour to organizations supporting Palestinians, following his removal from the tour due to backlash over his pro-Palestine stage remarks. The removal occurred after venue owners, including Patriots owner Robert Kraft, objected to his participation, prompting several other opening acts to withdraw in solidarity. Macklemore also challenged Kraft to match his donation, while figures like Colin Kaepernick criticized the venue owners for colluding to silence him.
key_points: Macklemore pledged his $1 million net earnings from Ed Sheeran's tour to organizations working with Palestinian people.
He was dropped from the tour after making pro-Palestine statements during a concert at MetLife Stadium.
New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft refused to let Macklemore perform at Gillette Stadium, citing past rhetoric.
All four remaining opening acts for Ed Sheeran's tour withdrew in solidarity with Macklemore.
Former NFL quarterback Colin Kaepernick criticized NFL owners, accusing them of colluding to protect their interests.

title: Colin Kaepernick says NFL owners are colluding against Macklemore after Ed Sheeran tour ban
author: Tom Lutz
content:
Colin Kaepernick has accused NFL owners of colluding against Macklemore after the rapper was removed from Ed Sheeran’s tour over comments he made onstage about Palestine.
Kaepernick, whose NFL career was effectively ended in the wake of his protests against police violence, says he sees parallels between himself and Macklemore.
“The part that I hope people appreciate and take away in this moment is what [New England Patriots owner] Robert Kraft and what they’re saying by denying Macklemore the opportunity to go out and perform with Ed Sheeran is they are willing to collude,” Kaepernick said on the MeidasTouch podcast. “The [NFL owners] are openly colluding.”
Macklemore had been a supporting act on Ed Sheeran’s tour. During an appearance at New Jersey’s MetLife stadium he told the crowd he wanted the people of Gaza and “the occupied West Bank” to know “we have not forgotten about them”. He also said “free Palestine”.
Kraft, who is a longtime supporter of Israel, and several other owners of NFL stadiums the tour was due to visit said they would not let Macklemore play at their venues. This prompted Macklemore to be removed from the tour. All four supporting acts for upcoming dates of Sheeran’s tour have since withdrawn in support of Macklemore.
During the 2016 NFL season, Kaepernick began kneeling during the national anthem in protest at police brutality and social injustice. Despite being in his prime, Kaepernick was not signed by any NFL team after he left the San Francisco 49ers at the end of that season, and he has not played in the league since. He filed a grievance against the NFL in 2017, and the case was settled in 2019 with terms of the agreement undisclosed.
Kaepernick told the MeidasTouch podcast that Kraft and other NFL owners had tried to hound out Macklemore in a similar way they did to him.
“When we filed the grievance, it was like, well, the owners wouldn’t do that,” Kaepernick said. “Everybody just wants to win within the NFL. And the realization is, no. They want to protect their interests. They want to protect their power. They want to protect their money. And they also want people to know that if you take an action that they don’t agree with, they will come for you.”
Kraft has said his decision to ban Macklemore from the Patriots’ stadium was due to his “recent actions” and “a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community”.
Kaepernick said others may find themselves in a similar situation to Macklemore in the future.
“It may not touch you today, at some point it’s going to come knocking on your doorstep or someone you love’s doorstep and that’s not the moment to be able to take action,” he said. “We should be taking action actively right now.”
Elsewhere on Wednesday, NBA star Kyrie Irving said he would pay a $11,492 fine the NFL gave to Azeez Al-Shair after he displayed the name of a Palestinian girl killed by Israel during a game. Al-Shair did so using a face marking banned by the league.
summary: Colin Kaepernick accused NFL owners, including Robert Kraft, of colluding against rapper Macklemore after he was banned from performing at NFL stadiums and removed from Ed Sheeran's tour. Macklemore was dropped after making pro-Palestinian remarks at a concert, prompting his fellow supporting acts to withdraw in solidarity. Kaepernick drew parallels between Macklemore's situation and his own NFL career, which stalled after he knelt during the national anthem to protest police brutality.
key_points: Colin Kaepernick stated that NFL owners are openly colluding to punish Macklemore.
Macklemore was removed from Ed Sheeran's tour after stadium owners, including Robert Kraft, banned him following his pro-Palestinian remarks.
Kraft cited Macklemore's recent actions and a history of offensive rhetoric regarding the Jewish community as the reason for the ban.
All four supporting acts for upcoming dates on Ed Sheeran's tour withdrew in support of Macklemore.
Kaepernick compared the situation to how his own NFL career ended after he protested police brutality in 2016.

title: Which artists have pulled out of Ed Sheeran’s tour over Palestine?
author: Al Jazeera Staff
content:
![Recording artist Macklemore appears on ABC's "Good Morning America" Summer Concert Series in Central Park in New York on July 22, 2022, left, and Ed Sheeran appears at the premiere of the film "F1 The Movie" in London on June 23, 2025. (AP Photo)](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/ap_6aa9b031c60a6-1789505585.jpg?resize=770%2C513&quality=80)
All supporting acts for English pop star Ed Sheeran’s upcoming US Loop Tour have quit in solidarity with rapper Macklemore, who was dropped from the tour for supporting Palestine.
Some of the other artists are Irish and have cited their own country’s historical experience of suffering under occupation as the reason for their opposition to Israel’s illegal occupation of the Palestinian territories.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items
- list 1 of 3Macklemore cut from Ed Sheeran tour for pro-Palestine stance
- list 2 of 3Who is Robert Kraft, pro-Israel billionaire who cancelled Macklemore?
- list 3 of 3Ed Sheeran blames US tour promoter for dropping Macklemore
Macklemore, whose real name is Ben Haggerty, drew criticism after saying “Free Palestine” and making other pro-Palestine comments while on tour with Sheeran at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey earlier this month.
He was ultimately dropped from the remainder of Sheeran’s tour, partly under pressure from the billionaire owner of one of the venues, the Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, Robert Kraft. On Tuesday, Sheeran blamed the tour’s US promoter.
“I was informed that this stance was based on how Macklemore conveyed part of this message during his performance, rather than on everything that was said,” Sheeran wrote. “I spoke with the venues at length all week to try and build a bridge.”
Who are the musicians and bands who have also quit the tour?
Which artists are pulling out and why?
In statements on their social media platforms shortly after Sheeran’s announcement, American singer-songwriter Finneas, Irish singer Aaron Rowe, Irish band Beoga and Danish pop band Lukas Graham announced they would be dropping out of the tour, which is scheduled to begin on September 19 in Philadelphia.
Sheeran is set to kick off his North American tour at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia on Saturday.
Finneas, US singer-songwriter
![Finneas O’Connell aka FINNEAS performs at Astra on May 2, 2025 in Berlin, Germany](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/GettyImages-2213108822-1789578261.jpg?w=770&resize=770%2C601&quality=80)
Finneas, who was scheduled to open for Sheeran in some American cities during the tour, announced on Instagram on Tuesday that he had decided to withdraw from the tour after Macklemore’s expulsion.
He and his sister, the multi-Grammy and Academy Award-winning pop singer Billie Eilish, have talked about their Irish family roots and have been outspoken about their support for Palestine before.
“Artists must not be silenced when they speak up for the oppressed,” he said on Instagram on Tuesday.
“I stand with Palestine and its people,” he added.
Aaron Rowe, Irish singer
![Aaron Rowe performs onstage during All Together Now Festival on August 02, 2025 in Waterford, Ireland](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/GettyImages-2228208790-1789578072.jpg?w=770&resize=770%2C513&quality=80)
On Tuesday, Rowe, who performed as part of Sheeran’s Australian leg of the tour earlier this year and was to do 10 more dates in the US, said he has also decided to withdraw.
“I don’t take the decision lightly,” he said on Instagram.
“Ed has been a friend to me and has changed my life, I could never thank him enough for this,” he acknowledged.
“But as Irish people, we know all too well about genocide, forced famine and violent occupation. I cannot stand by and allow billionaires to use their position of power to silence the rightful voices of those who speak up against Israeli genocide and who highlight the savage murder of children. I would lose all respect for myself to carry on as normal,” he added.
Beoga, Irish band
Beoga is Sheeran’s backing band. Yet on Tuesday, the group announced on Instagram that it would also quit the US leg of the tour “following the silencing of Macklemore by zionist lobbies”.
“We are a traditional Irish band who never saw ourselves playing in stadiums of that size and that opportunity is not lost on us. We have been friends with Ed for over 10 years now and will continue to be. We believe in dialogue as a means of progressing the plight of the Palestinian people,” they added.
Lukas Graham, Danish band
![The Danish band Lukas Graham performs at Tinderbox music festival in Odense, Denmark, June 27, 2025](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/2025-06-27T191636Z_1386193349_RC25BFABXDJF_RTRMADP_3_DENMARK-ENTERTAINMENT-1789578483.jpg?w=770&resize=770%2C513&quality=80)
Announcing their withdrawal from the tour in an Instagram statement on Tuesday, lead singer Lukas Forchhammer wrote: “It’s hard to watch families in other parts of the world burying the people they love. We should be able to speak about war, about civilians being killed, about children who deserve to grow up. Wherever they live. Whatever flag flies over them.”
“Money doesn’t give you the right to own the conversation. Nobody’s bank balance should decide who gets to speak or which suffering we’re allowed to acknowledge,” he said.
How did the Macklemore controversy start?
Macklemore opened a Sheeran show at the New Jersey MetLife Stadium earlier this month with a speech about Palestine.
He said: “The people all the way in Gaza to the occupied West Bank know that we have not forgotten about them. I say free Palestine. I say free Lebanon. Free Cuba to the Congo to Sudan to Iran.”
The speech triggered an immediate backlash, and the Israeli-American Council started a petition to have Macklemore dropped from the tour.
Macklemore defended his statements, and also his performance of the song Hind’s Hall – dedicated to Hind Rajab, the five-year-old girl killed by Israeli forces while stranded inside a car in Gaza – by stating that “wanting all humans to be treated equal should never be controversial”.
Hamilton Hall, one of the main buildings on the campus of Columbia University, was the site of a student protest in 2024 against Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza. The students occupied the hall and renamed it “Hind’s Hall”.
How did Robert Kraft get involved in the row?
In an Instagram post, Macklemore told fans: “Ed [Sheeran] told me that [Robert] Kraft said I would not be allowed to perform in his stadium.”
He also claimed that Sheeran told him Kraft had rallied other stadium owners, who collectively issued an ultimatum: “If Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues.”
Kraft defended his involvement in preventing Macklemore from performing at his own stadium in a statement. He said, “This decision is not about diminishing the suffering of innocent Palestinians or denying anyone the right to advocate on their behalf.”
“But that advocacy should not come at the expense of the Jewish community or obscure the responsibility of Hamas … whose horrific actions have caused immeasurable suffering for Palestinians and Israelis alike.”
Kraft’s public statement on the issue did not address the claim that the billionaire lobbied other stadium owners. He did say he would be happy to sit down with Macklemore and talk in person.
What has Ed Sheeran said?
Sheeran posted his response to the row on Instagram on Tuesday, confirming that Macklemore had been removed because of his pro-Palestinian stance, but denying that he was responsible.
He wrote: “I am appalled by the conflict between Israel and Palestine. The suffering and pain caused on both sides is a human tragedy. There are too many wars across the world causing immeasurable pain, none of which should be tolerated. Macklemore asked to join my tour last year and I agreed, because I respect him as an artist. As with all my support acts, I agree that they play a setlist of their choosing.
“After Macklemore’s performances at my New Jersey shows, venues on my upcoming tour dates communicated that they would pull the shows if he was still supporting. I was informed that this stance was based on how Macklemore conveyed part of his message during his performance, rather than on everything that was said. I spoke with the venues at length all week to try and build a bridge. One of those people was Robert Kraft. I was also involved in direct talks with promoters along with activists on both sides to try and find a mutual resolution for all, but the venue’s and promoter’s decision was final.
“Macklemore coming off tour was the promoter’s decision; it was not mine. Macklemore’s contract for the tour was with the promoter, not me.
“I would never let down the fans who had made plans, nor would I abandon the touring crew and the other support acts and musicians who rely on me for work and to make a living.”
How did others react?
While Sheeran and the tour’s operators have yet to comment on the supporting acts quitting, Macklemore, climate activist Greta Thunberg, the musicians, fans and supporters of Palestine and Gaza, have all lauded the artists for their decision to quit the tour.
Macklemore has commented on each of their Instagram posts with a heart and the Palestinian flag.
Some Instagram users who had not heard some of the artists, such as Rowe, before left comments such as, “You’ve gained a fan.”
Commenting on Finneas’s post, the Europe Palestine network, a civil society initiative, said: “What is happening is HUGE !!! Artists turning their back to billionaires !!! I am so happy and proud !!!!”
Sheeran has faced criticism on social media for allowing Macklemore to be barred from performing.
In a video rant against Sheeran, Belgium-based filmmaker and activist Thomas Maddens said that one of Sheeran’s songs, “What Do I Know” in 2017, includes the lyric, “The Revolution is coming, it’s a minute away. I saw people marching in the streets today.”
Maddens noted that, despite this song, Sheeran apparently sided with the people who are not marching [for Palestine].
Addressing Sheeran in his video, he added: “When it is white people you march with them. But when it is brown people, you don’t seem to care very much.”
While Macklemore did not blame his longtime friend Sheeran for the debacle and described him as “apolitical”, the latter has performed at a charity concert to raise money for Ukraine, and he has also recorded a music video with the Ukrainian military rock band Antytila.
Pink Floyd cofounder Roger Waters, who has also been vocal about his support for Palestine, said on his social media: “There are two kinds of people in this world.”
“Some people do the right thing. That rapper, Macklemore, would be one of those people.” he said.
Referring to Sheeran, he said: “And there are people who are p***ks, like you, who do the wrong thing. Goodbye.”
summary: Multiple supporting acts have withdrawn from Ed Sheeran's upcoming US tour in solidarity with rapper Macklemore, who was dropped from the lineup following pro-Palestine remarks at a New Jersey concert. Artists including Finneas, Aaron Rowe, Beoga, and Lukas Graham cited freedom of speech and opposition to the occupation of Palestinian territories as reasons for their departure. While venue owner Robert Kraft defended his decision regarding the tour stops, Sheeran stated that Macklemore's removal was ultimately the decision of the US tour promoter and venues.
key_points: Rapper Macklemore was removed from Ed Sheeran's US tour following pro-Palestine comments made during a concert at MetLife Stadium.
Supporting acts Finneas, Aaron Rowe, Beoga, and Lukas Graham announced they are quitting the tour in solidarity with Macklemore.
Several withdrawing artists cited their opposition to Israeli occupation and the silencing of voices speaking out for Palestinians.
Ed Sheeran stated that Macklemore's removal was decided by the US tour promoter and venues, not by himself.

title: Katie Price’s husband makes bizarre offer to TV hosts from Dubai prison
author: Rachel McGrath
content:
Katie Price’s jailed husband offers to send GMB hosts £10k in cryptocurrency after TV star confirms split

Katie Price’s husband makes bizarre offer to TV hosts from Dubai prison
- Katie Price's estranged husband, Lee Andrews, offered to transfer Good Morning Britain hosts Ed Balls and Susanna Reid up to £10,000 in a bizarre WhatsApp voice note sent to the ITV show.

Andrews canceled a joint studio appearance regarding claims that he lied about being a crypto-multimillionaire after Price discovered only £2.22 in his wallet. During her appearance on the show, Price confirmed their split and stated that she felt scammed by him.

Andrews claimed he could not appear on Good Morning Britain because he is being held in a Dubai prison over unpaid debts.
Price revealed she discovered Andrews's crypto wallet contained only £2.22, leading to accusations that he lied about his wealth.
