title: Practical Magic 2 star: 'People long for simpler times'
author: Naomi Clarke
content:
![Joey King and Maisie Williams attend the Practical Magic 2 European Premiere in London. Joey wears a cream dress with a lace overlay and flower details and her red hair is worn down in waves. Maisie wears a red dress and her brunette hair in an updo.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1280/cpsprodpb/bcdf/live/d9d20260-ac56-11f1-9e64-05835b0b18f8.jpg)
Actresses Joey King and Maisie Williams are joining the cast of the sequel to portray the daughters of Sandra Bullock's character
- Published
Mix together a beloved film simmering for decades, a sprinkling of social media hype and a generous glug of star power and you just might conjure up the long-awaited sequel to Practical Magic.
The 1998 fantasy romcom, starring Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman as witchy sisters Sally and Gillian Owens, received mixed reviews from critics when it was first released.
But it's put a spell on a new generation discovering it online, with some now regarding the film as a cult classic and autumn staple.
The demand for a follow-up by this new wave of fans helped convince Bullock and Kidman to reprise their roles nearly 30 years on, they say.
"You never get the opportunity to do something where people really are asking you, 'please do it'," says Bullock. "It's usually us going to them."
Actresses Joey King and Maisie Williams are joining the cast this time round to play Sally's daughters, Kylie and Antonia.
Kissing Booth star King tells BBC Newsbeat she feels this desire for nostalgic content, which has become one of the defining forces within entertainment in recent years, has been influenced by "the world moving so fast".
![Maisie Williams, Nicole Kidman, Sandra Bullock and Joey King attend the US premiere of  Practical Magic 2.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/8420/live/337e1310-aba5-11f1-8e72-a346833ed029.jpg)
Practical Magic 2 sees the cast return to a world which is steeped in powerful ancestral magic
"I think with technology moving at the speed that it is, we're really missing the times when we were less reachable," she says.
"If we couldn't figure out something, we'd stare out the window until it came to us, and I think we're nostalgic for a time like that."
She feels this can also be a strength of cinema as it can help "make memories" and "feelings" for people that they can revisit by rewatching.
The upcoming release comes at a time when reboots, reunions and remakes are dominating film and TV lists.
Game of Thrones star Williams agrees the drive for nostalgic content feels like a "symptom of people longing for simpler times", but says she is "very grateful" that they have made a sequel and not a remake.
"I do believe in pushing the story forwards and I do believe in telling new stories," she says.
"And I do believe stories can come back around and they can still be meaningful.
"But I am not the biggest fan of the remake because I think it's a shame to withhold ourselves from telling a new story."
![Sandra Bullock, Maisie Williams, Joey King and Nicole Kidman portraying their Practical Magic 2 characters Sally, Antonia, Kylie and Gillian Owens.  They are standing on top of a building holding umbrellas in the air and wearing dresses.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2048/cpsprodpb/04e1/live/e639edb0-ac60-11f1-be57-03729df1d736.jpg)
The bond of sisterhood is at the heart of the 1998 film and continues into the sequel
Practical Magic 2 sees the cast return to a world which is steeped in powerful ancestral magic with the characters once again confronting a family curse which condemns anyone who loves and is loved by an Owens woman to death.
There are also nods to the original throughout, with bubbling family tension, dark romantic "witchcore" fashion and the iconic midnight margaritas.
US acting stalwarts Dianne Wiest and Stockard Channing return to their roles for the follow-up, while Guardians of the Galaxy actor Lee Pace, Cobra Kai's Xolo MaridueÃ±a and House of the Dragon's Solly McLeod are new additions.
Reviews so far have been mixed, with the Guardian describing it as a "nostalgia-bait return", external which is as "strange and messy as the first" but with "warm seasonal pleasures to be had".
Meanwhile The Hollywood Reporter, external says the "slapdash" sequel "works better the less you look for any sense of logic, and the more you just lean into the transient joys of watching these actresses bounce off each other".
![Joey King portraying Sallyâs daughters Kylie. She is looking at her hand which is outstretched as a mist is wafting off of it.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/cc02/live/50207ba0-ac60-11f1-be57-03729df1d736.jpg)
Joey King says the idea of "being witchy" can be "empowering right now"
Amid the scrutiny around the film, Williams admits joining the Practical Magic world was "a little bit overwhelming", but says the cast were "so supportive the whole time" and "welcomed us into the sisterhood".
The bond of sisterhood is at the heart of the first film and continues in the sequel, but Bullock has recalled this was initially one of the criticisms of the original, external, with some branding it as "too witchy" with "too many women".
With women's rights under pressure in some countries, Williams says it is a "challenging time" and she feels it's "so important in a time like this for women to be supporting one another".
"We are in a time when young women are staying in education longer and women, before having children, are sometimes being paid more than their male counterparts, which I do find to be really exciting," she adds.
"But there's a lot of work to do.
"And this feeling of witches, symbiosis and power - I feel like there's something in that which can just push us forwards."
![A footer logo for BBC Newsbeat. It has the BBC logo and the word Newsbeat in white over a colorful background of violet, purple and orange shapes. At the bottom a black square reading "Listen on Sounds" is visible.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/976/cpsprodpb/e185/live/c8857230-14f0-11ef-976f-87c9f89e656e.jpg)
summary: Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman are reprising their roles in the long-awaited sequel Practical Magic 2, driven by demand from a new generation of fans. Actresses Joey King and Maisie Williams join the cast as Sally's daughters in a story that continues to explore ancestral magic and the bond of sisterhood. The cast and crew attribute the demand for the sequel to a broader cultural longing for simpler times amidst fast-moving technology.
key_points: Practical Magic 2 brings back original stars Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman nearly 30 years after the 1998 fantasy romcom.
Joey King and Maisie Williams join the cast to portray Sally's daughters, Kylie and Antonia.
Cast members believe the demand for nostalgic reboots reflects people longing for simpler times and less reachable technology.
The sequel retains core elements from the original film, including ancestral magic, family curses, and themes of sisterhood.

title: 'RuPaul's Drag Race UK' Canceled By The BBC Amid "Financial Pressures"
author: Jake Kanter
content:
![Drag Race UK](https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/p07rmcp1.jpg?w=681&h=383&crop=1) 
RuPaul’s Drag Race UK has reached the end of the runway on the BBC.
The BBC has decided not to renew Drag Race UK beyond Season 8 this year, citing “financial pressures” as the UK broadcaster seeks savings of £500 million ($677 million).
Producer World of Wonder plans to pivot the show, as well as spin-off series, to its streaming service, Wow Presents Plus, promising a “new era” for the franchise.
A BBC spokesperson said: “As the BBC continues to navigate significant financial pressures and deliver the savings required of us, we have had to make some very difficult choices, none of which have been taken lightly.
“We can therefore confirm together with World of Wonder, that RuPaul’s Drag Race UK will be leaving the BBC and moving to Wow Presents Plus. The BBC is incredibly proud of all eleven series of this groundbreaking show and we would like to thank RuPaul, World of Wonder and everyone involved, both on and off screen.”
Watch on Deadline
Featuring judges RuPaul, Michelle Visage, Graham Norton and Alan Carr, Drag Race has averaged around 1.5 million viewers, according to BBC News.
Drag Race UK is the latest show to fall victim to cuts after the BBC canceled Blankety Blank, Celebrity Mastermind, and Live At The Apollo in July.
summary: The BBC has canceled 'RuPaul's Drag Race UK' beyond Season 8 due to financial pressures as the broadcaster seeks to save £500 million. Producer World of Wonder will move the main show and its spin-offs to its streaming service, Wow Presents Plus. The series averaged around 1.5 million viewers and joins other BBC cuts including Blankety Blank and Celebrity Mastermind.
key_points: The BBC decided not to renew 'RuPaul's Drag Race UK' beyond Season 8.
Financial pressures and a required £500 million in savings drove the decision.
World of Wonder plans to move the franchise to the Wow Presents Plus streaming service.
The show joins other BBC programs such as Celebrity Mastermind and Live At The Apollo in being canceled.

title: Strictly: New hosts explain their roles as they reject 'roving presenter' reports
author: Helen Bushby
content:
![Johannes Radebe, Josh Widdicombe and Emma Willis smiling together in smart, presenting clothes](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/eccb/live/d5b3ae30-ad1f-11f1-826f-933990eae6f0.jpg)
Johannes Radebe, Josh Widdicombe and Emma Willis said their presenting roles are "kind of open" and not defined
- Published
Emma Willis, Josh Widdicombe and Johannes Radebe have said they will not have "fixed roles" on Strictly Come Dancing, as they prepare to replace Tess Daly and Claudia Winkleman later this month.
Daly and Winkleman left the programme together at the end of the 2025 series.
Daly was the host on the dancefloor, introducing the dancers and judges, while Winkleman did the post-dance debrief upstairs in the "Clauditorium".
"No one's replacing anybody - at the minute it's all very kind of open," Willis told Richard Osman on The Rest is Entertainment podcast.
They also scotched reports of Radebe having a "roving reporter" role , externalon the show, with Willis saying: "There's definitely no backstage roving reporter, which is what has been reported quite a bit."
Widdicombe added that they would "be like Total Football" [where players can take the role of anyone on the team], adding: "We're going to be moving everywhere".
Radebe added he will definitely be doing "a little bit of prying and finding out the truth", having been a professional dancer on the show, with the advantage of knowing everyone on it really well already.
He called his new role "very, very exciting," although he admitted he felt a "little bit of a tinge" of FOMO [fear of missing out] at seeing the pros in rehearsals.
They also added that the plan to put the three of them together was a "wild card decision" by producers, which took them all by surprise.
Willis explained the audition process, saying they had to do a "chemistry test" to see how they interacted as a group.
She said they were told: "This is the last one and this is a wild card. We're just like, 'What happens if we do three?'
"And they said, 'It's so much of a wild card, we don't really have a script for you either.
"'So we're going to sit down, get it up on the screen and we'll have a little tinker all together'."
![Dancers and judges on the Strictly Christmas show salute outgoing presenters Claudia Winkleman and Tess Daly, seen dressed in all white](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/848/cpsprodpb/49f6/live/3a3205d0-e0b3-11f0-902d-59ae24c9d070.jpg)
Claudia Winkleman and Tess Daly said farewell to the show together last year
Willis called the hiring process "the most cloak and dagger thing" she has ever seen, saying it took about four months in total and that the chemistry test was "terrifying, but so brilliant".
Widdecombe added that it was all so secretive that he had to tell his taxi driver he was testing for a show called The Great Garden Glow Up, if he was asked.
They all joked about how the three of them appear as a group, with Osman saying to Willis: "You and Johannes look good together."
Widdecombe responded: " Do you know what I have realised? It's difficult when you're paired with two of the most striking people on television."
Osman then quipped: "You do look a bit like a competition winner," to which Widdecombe agreed.
![Karen Carney and Carlos Gu with their trophy after winning the 2025 series of Strictly Come Dancing.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/999/cpsprodpb/0394/live/77cc0dc0-ddeb-11f0-aae2-2191c0e48a3b.jpg)
Former footballer Karen Carney and dancer Carlos Gu won last year's giltterball trophy
Radebe also admitted he will "struggle" with having to be impartial now he is not longer competing.
Osman asked him if the gloves would be off should the judges get overly critical of the new crop of contestants, and the dancer joked he was "waiting for that judges' debrief".
The show is returning with 15 celebrities competing for the glitterball trophy, including Australian singer Delta Goodrem, former England footballer Shaun Wright-Phillips, actresses Lacey Turner and Jaime Winstone and Team GB skeleton racer Tabby Stoecker.
Judges Shirley Ballas, Revel Horwood, Motsi Mabuse, and Anton Du Beke are also back for the new series, which starts on Saturday 19 September.
summary: Emma Willis, Josh Widdicombe, and Johannes Radebe are set to replace Tess Daly and Claudia Winkleman as the new hosts of Strictly Come Dancing. The trio clarified that they will not have fixed roles, rejecting reports of a backstage roving presenter, and instead comparing their dynamic to Total Football. Their selection followed a secretive four-month audition process that involved a group chemistry test described as a wild card decision by producers.
key_points: Emma Willis, Josh Widdicombe, and Johannes Radebe are the new presenters for Strictly Come Dancing.
The hosts rejected reports that Radebe would serve as a roving reporter.
The trio stated they will not have fixed roles and will be moving everywhere on the show.
The hiring process involved a secret group chemistry test after producers made a wild card decision to use three hosts.
The new series is scheduled to start on Saturday 19 September with returning judges and 15 competing celebrities.

title: ‘RuPaul’s Drag Race UK’ Dropped by BBC
author: Lily Ford
content:
!['RuPaul's Drag Race UK'](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/FotoJet-2026-09-10T093618.604.jpg?w=1920&h=1080&crop=1) 
RuPaul’s Drag Race UK, you may now sashay away.
After eight seasons, the beloved British spinoff of RuPaul’s franchise-spawning competition has been dropped by the BBC, with the broadcaster citing “significant financial pressures.” In April, the BBC announced a plan to cut 1,800 staffers in a bid to save £500 million ($678m).
A representative told The Hollywood Reporter on Thursday: “As the BBC continues to navigate significant financial pressures and deliver the savings required of us, we have had to make some very difficult choices, none of which have been taken lightly.”
Related Stories
!['Drawn Together' film still](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/wp-content/themes/vip/pmc-hollywoodreporter-2021/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif) 
![Actress Emilia Schuele on her way to attend the official Dior event. Photographed by the Honor Robot Phone.](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/wp-content/themes/vip/pmc-hollywoodreporter-2021/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif) 
The series currently runs on BBC Three and iPlayer. The rep continued that future shows — and its spin-off, RuPaul’s Drag Race UK Vs The World — will instead be broadcast on Wow Presents Plus, a platform owned by Drag Race UK production company World of Wonder.
“The BBC is incredibly proud of all eleven series of this groundbreaking show and we would like to thank RuPaul, World of Wonder and everyone involved, both on and off screen,” the rep added. “We are certain that viewers will enjoy the eighth [season].”
Since 2019, Drag Race UK has catapulted some of the biggest drag queens in Britain to stratospheric stardom, launching the careers of Baga Chipz, Bimini Bon-Boulash, Tayce and The Vivienne. Tia Kofi went on to become a member of the Eurovision presenting team, La Voix featured on EastEnders and Strictly Come Dancing, and Ginger Johnson won Celebrity MasterChef last year.
The format involves amateur and professional drag queens competing in a series of challenges to win over judges RuPaul, Michelle Visage, Graham Norton and Alan Carr, and celebrity guest judges such as Jade Thirlwall, Lucy Punch, Hannah Waddingham, Andrew Garfield, Anne-Marie, Thandiwe Newton and Cat Burns.
At its peak, per BBC News, the show averaged around 1.5 million viewers per episode. Viewers will be able to continue watching existing seasons of RuPaul’s Drag Race UK and RuPaul’s Drag Race UK Vs on BBC iPlayer.
summary: The BBC has dropped "RuPaul's Drag Race UK" after eight seasons due to significant financial pressures and required savings. Future episodes and its spin-off, "RuPaul's Drag Race UK Vs The World," will now air on Wow Presents Plus, a platform owned by production company World of Wonder. Existing seasons will remain available for viewers on BBC iPlayer.
key_points: "RuPaul's Drag Race UK" has been dropped by the BBC after eight seasons.
The broadcaster cited significant financial pressures and a plan to cut 1,800 staffers and save £500 million.
Future series will be broadcast on World of Wonder's platform, Wow Presents Plus.
Existing seasons will continue to be available to watch on BBC iPlayer.

title: Harry Styles extends tour, with Kylie as a support act
author: Mark Savage
content:
![Harry Styles on stage in Wembley](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/abef/live/87cccb20-ad15-11f1-826f-933990eae6f0.jpg)
Harry Styles set a new world record with his residency at Wembley Stadium this summer
- Published
Harry Styles is extending his record-breaking Together, Together tour in 2027, with 25 more shows, including a return to Wembley Stadium next August.
The singer, who is currently in the middle of a 30-show residency at New York's Madison Square Garden, is adding dates in Ireland, Spain, Italy, Germany and France - who all missed out on the tour's first leg this summer.
Every city will see a different support act, with 80s pop icons Tears For Fears playing at Wembley, and pop legend Kylie Minogue on the bill in Los Angeles.
Although Minogue is a festival headliner in Europe, these shows will represent her first ever stadium concerts in the US.
She celebrated the announcement on her Instagram stories, writing: "Together, together. Harry. Me. Can't wait to see you in April, LA."
![Harry Styles on stage in Amsterdam](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/74a1/live/626eb980-ad18-11f1-826f-933990eae6f0.jpg)
The tour opened in Amsterdam in May
Unlike the first half of the tour, which concentrated on long residencies in cities like London and New York, the 2027 dates represent a more traditional rolling stage show.
Styles will also play US stadiums for the first time as a solo artist - with dates booked in Phoenix, Dallas, Atlanta and Chicago.
After confusion and outcry over ticket prices for the 2026 shows, the singer's team have made the pricing structure clear for his upcoming dates, specifying that prices will range from $60 to $300 (Â£44 to Â£221).
The 2027 dates will also introduce "Unpredictable Fun Tickets," an initiative to make concerts more accessible to people on a limited income.
The programme will make a limited number of tickets available for Â£20 in the UK, $20 in the US and â¬20 in Europe. Details on availability and how to apply will be announced soon.
The cost of regular tickets will vary by city. Details, including on-sale dates, are available on the star's website., external
![Harry Styles fans](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/e04e/live/d437c0c0-ad18-11f1-826f-933990eae6f0.jpg)
Almost one million people attended the Wembley shows, travelling from all over the world to see the former One Direction star
Fans were already aware that a second leg of Styles' tour was on the way, after the 32-year-old posted a note on Wednesday teasing what he called the "final" shows of the hugely-successful run.
"When we decided to do the 2026 tour I knew it would be special but what you turned it into was far beyond what I could have imagined," he wrote.
"I love playing music, I love being with all of you and being a part of the love and joy you all create together every night. That's why I wanted you to be the first to know we will be adding 2027 dates, which honestly, at first I found daunting.
"Being an artist is the only life I've ever known really, I have been doing this since I was 16 years old, and I feel like the luckiest person in the world to still be sharing these moments with you.
"Tomorrow's announcement will be the final cities of Together, Together," he continued.
"After that, I don't know what comes next for me, but I know that I'm excited to find out."
![Harry Styles on stage](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/e802/live/fe559d00-ad18-11f1-826f-933990eae6f0.jpg)
The singer is donating money from his UK shows to support grassroots venues
Reviews for the Together, Together tour have been largely positive.
Rolling Stone magazine called Styles "effortlessly charismatic" , externaland noted there was "real diversity" in a setlist that covered all four of his solo albums to date.
Variety magazine was also impressed by his stage presence, external, writing: "Styles is a one-in-millions performer, with a hurricane-force charm that's dashing and sexy and goofy at the same time."
The BBC's own review noted the unique stage design, which carved Wembley into smaller fan zones, making the event "more like a club show than a stadium concert - with Styles zipping around the borders, blowing kisses and posing for cameras throughout the night".
Styles' 12-night stint at the venue earned him a Guinness World Record for the longest residency by a musician at Wembley Stadium during a single run.
He will wrap up the tour with three further nights at the stadium next August. Â£1 from every ticket sold in London will be donated to the Live Trust, which aims to support and protect grassroots music in the UK.
summary: Harry Styles has announced an extension of his Together, Together tour for 2027, adding 25 new shows including his first solo US stadium dates and a return to Wembley Stadium. The upcoming leg features various support acts, such as Tears For Fears in London and Kylie Minogue in Los Angeles. To address previous pricing concerns, his team established clear ticket prices ranging from $60 to $300 alongside a low-cost ticket accessibility program.
key_points: Harry Styles is adding 25 dates to his Together, Together tour for 2027, including stops in Ireland, Spain, Italy, Germany, France, and the US.
Kylie Minogue will support Styles in Los Angeles for what will be her first-ever stadium concerts in the US.
Regular ticket prices will range from $60 to $300, and a new 'Unpredictable Fun Tickets' initiative will offer limited tickets for 20 in local currencies.
Styles will wrap up the tour with three nights at Wembley Stadium next August, donating £1 from every London ticket to the Live Trust for grassroots music.

title: John Major’s rise from obscure whip to PM part of new National Theatre season
author: Nadia Khomami
content:
A new play about John Major’s rise to power, written by James Graham, will premiere at the National Theatre in London next year, as part of a season that puts political upheaval and global conflict at the heart of its programme.
Major reunites Graham with Jeremy Herrin, the director behind the acclaimed parliamentary drama This House. It will chart Major’s emergence from relatively obscure whip to prime minister, taking over from Margaret Thatcher at a pivotal moment in Britain’s relationship with Europe.
The National Theatre said the play would explore what leadership means at times of political change, with Graham returning to the recent political history that has become a recurring subject of his work.
![Uzo Aduba b](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/0630012fe1067a2e14e270e3a4ef088f54154a28/0_330_4480_5600/master/4480.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
It is one of eight world premieres announced by the theatre for next year, with a programme that its director, Indhu Rubasingham, said would examine “the perspectives, cultures and conflicts that continue to shape our world”.
Also on the programme is The Great Indaba, written by Moira Buffini and directed by Rubasingham, which dramatises an extraordinary 1997 meeting in South Africa involving Nelson Mandela’s new national unity government and political rivals from Northern Ireland, as the Good Friday agreement negotiations approached a breakthrough.
Another new play, Samira, by Carmen Nasr, is set during the Arab Spring and will be directed by Emily Burns. The Adeyemis – A Family Saga, a new political family drama by the British Nigerian writer Oladipo Agboluaje, will have its world premiere in the Dorfman theatre, directed by Lucian Msamati and starring Uzo Aduba.
Among the season’s other new work is Mr Loverman, Natasha Gordon’s stage adaptation of Bernardine Evaristo’s acclaimed novel about a married Caribbean man confronting his sexuality. Gary Beadle, Jo Martin and Danny Sapani are among the initial cast, with Paulette Randall directing.
There is also a new British musical, Glorious Madness, featuring songs by Joan Armatrading, with a book by Iman Qureshi and directed by Phyllida Lloyd.
![Head a shoulders of Emilia Clarke](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/ca7b67855a808010939edf2d9287fe88cb074861/0_0_1024_1280/master/1024.jpg?width=120&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
The multi-award-winning theatre company Punchdrunk open a new immersive production called Ghostlight, conceived and directed by founder and artistic director Felix Barrett and curated by writer Lucy Kirkwood.
The programme is not without established works, but the balance is notable. Rather than a season dominated by Shakespeare and the traditional theatrical canon, the National has announced a series of modern classics and 20th-century works: West Side Story, co-directed by Marianne Elliott and Miranda Cromwell; Tennessee Williams’ Suddenly Last Summer, directed by Michael Grandage and starring Emma Corrin and Harriet Walter; David Hare’s Plenty, directed by former National Theatre director Richard Eyre and starring Emilia Clarke; and Death of a Salesman, starring Paul Mescal and Tracy Letts.
Tom Murphy’s A Whistle in the Dark and Tom Stoppard’s Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead will also return to the stage, with Mescal leading a repertory production alongside Death of a Salesman.
Notably, however, there is no Shakespeare production among the National’s three main stages in the new season. Hamlet will instead be among new titles added to the National Theatre Collection, the organisation’s streaming and education service.
![The National’s director Indhu Rubasingham and Kate Varah](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/033463676d5ceac72f39e047bb871238ba6d13d4/0_525_3744_2993/master/3744.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
The National says the 2027 programme will include 18 productions, eight of them world premieres, alongside touring productions and work reaching audiences through cinema, streaming and schools.
Rubasingham said the season was united by “themes of resilience and hope” and was intended to reflect “the international spirit at the heart of our National Theatre”.
Kate Varah, the theatre’s executive and co-chief executive, said the programme represented an investment in “original storytelling” and in “bold artistic voices”, at a time when theatre was increasingly reaching audiences beyond its South Bank stages.
summary: The National Theatre in London has announced a new season featuring eight world premieres, including a play by James Graham about John Major's rise to prime minister. The upcoming programme focuses on political upheaval, global conflict, and modern classics rather than traditional Shakespeare productions on its main stages. Additional highlights include new works by Moira Buffini, Carmen Nasr, Oladipo Agboluaje, Natasha Gordon, and Iman Qureshi, alongside star-studded revivals.
key_points: A new play by James Graham about John Major will premiere at the National Theatre.
The new season features eight world premieres focusing on political upheaval and global conflict.
There are no Shakespeare productions scheduled across the National Theatre's three main stages for the season.
The upcoming programme includes star-studded revivals of modern classics and 20th-century works starring actors like Emilia Clarke and Paul Mescal.

title: Harry blames King’s letter for Uganda’s withdrawal from Invictus Games
author: Victoria Ward; Ben Farmer
content:
![They sit together in a sports stadium stand](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/royal-family/2026/09/09/TELEMMGLPICT000293088617_17889572176580_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqplGOf-dgG3z4gg9owgQTXF5NUcTKNHKqy85KLqtvPLE.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![They sit together in a sports stadium stand](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/royal-family/2026/09/09/TELEMMGLPICT000293088617_17889572176580_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqplGOf-dgG3z4gg9owgQTXF5NUcTKNHKqy85KLqtvPLE.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
The Duke of Sussex has blamed Uganda’s decision to pull out of the Invictus Games on the King’s letter that described them as “private citizens”.
Uganda withdrew from Prince Harry’s international event for sick and injured military personnel on Wednesday, claiming it did not have the King’s “approval”.
The extraordinary move was announced by Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, the country’s military chief and son of the Ugandan president, who blamed the “Harry and Meghan nonsense”.
It came just two days after Buckingham Palace circulated a letter on the direction of the King confirming that the Duke and Duchess of Sussex were “private citizens” and that their work was not on behalf of the monarchy.
A source close to the Sussexes told The Telegraph on Wednesday evening that they believed the letter was to blame.
“Intended or unintended, this is clearly a consequence of the Lord Chamberlain’s guidance regarding the Duke and Duchess of Sussex that was rushed out without consultation on Monday,” the source said.
“Sadly, the only people who will suffer are the Invictus Games competitors.”
Gen Kainerugaba had earlier written on X: “In order not to be construed as being opposed to His Majesty King Charles III of the United Kingdom, whom we deeply revere, Uganda hereby withdraws from the invictus games. We shall not participate in anything that does not have His Majesty’s approval.”
![He wears a walrus moustache and military uniform](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/royal-family/2026/09/09/TELEMMGLPICT000501833424_17889574115040_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqA7N2CxnJWnYI3tCbVBgu9T0aesusvN1TE7a0ddd_esI.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
He told The Times: “I have factions in the ministry of defence that support that Harry-Meghan nonsense. I had to quash it straight away. I support the monarch. Period.”
The Invictus Games Foundation was unaware of the development before Gen Kainerugaba’s post was published on social media, The Telegraph understands. The organisation is now in discussions with its partners in Uganda to clarify the position.
In response, a Buckingham Palace source insisted that the King encouraged all organisations and endeavours in support of wounded service personnel.
Fears were immediately raised that Uganda’s decision was prompted by the letter circulated by the Lord Chamberlain, head of the royal household, on the direction of the King.
‘Duke and Duchess do not represent the sovereign’
The letter was sent to a small number of “key stakeholders” in Government and the military, specifying that the Duke and Duchess did not represent the sovereign, and were not working members of the Royal family.
It said the couple’s use of their HRH titles would remain in abeyance and that any charity work was “a personal matter for them both and undertaken in their private capacity”.
The letter added: “In short, their position is akin to private citizens with commercial and charitable interests.”
This marked the first sign of tension between the two camps since the pair returned to the UK with their two children last month.
The Sussexes admitted they were “surprised” not to have been given more than an hour’s advance notice of its circulation.
It was made public on the eve of a crunch meeting that is expected to decide whether or not the Sussexes are entitled to taxpayer-funded police protection now they are back in the UK.
The all-important Royal and VIP Executive Committee (Ravec) meeting is scheduled to take place this week, marking the climax of a deeply personal battle that Prince Harry has fought for more than six years.
Gen Kainerugaba, who is widely expected to follow in the footsteps of his 81-year-old father, Yoweri Museveni, is sometimes known as the “tweeting general” for his fiery and provocative posts.
In 2022, Mr Museveni was forced to step in and apologise after his son posted a series of messages threatening to invade neighbouring Kenya.
![Speaking into a microphone, he wears a broad-brimmed hat and gesticulates](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/royal-family/2026/09/09/TELEMMGLPICT000500478219_17889574917780_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqpVlberWd9EgFPZtcLiMQf0Rf_Wk3V23H2268P_XkPxc.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Gen Kainerugaba was also condemned for posts that were subsequently deleted, in which he threatened to have Bobi Wine, a defeated opposition candidate, castrated.
The general has stepped down from the social media platform at least twice, but has returned each time.
Uganda only joined the Invictus Games in July, becoming the 26th nation to take part and the first country from East Africa.
Its involvement was announced at an event at Chatham House in London, as Prince Harry began the one-year countdown to the Invictus Games 2027.
He was joined at the reception by Kiryowa Kiwanuka, Uganda’s defence minister, who praised the Duke.
Mr Kiwanuka said: “This milestone reflects our shared commitment to wounded, injured and sick servicemen and women who have sacrificed greatly in service to our nation.”
The minister said the decision to take part affirmed Uganda’s belief that “those who have borne the burdens of service deserve every opportunity to rebuild their lives with dignity, purpose, and hope”. “They are our living heroes,” he added.
The Duke posed for a picture with Ugandan delegates, raising a laugh as he held up a cardboard plaque the size of a tea tray and pretended to throw it like a Frisbee across the room.
The about-turn announced by Gen Kainerugaba will come as a blow to Prince Harry, who has recently moved back to Britain and plans to make the build-up to next year’s Games, which will take place in Birmingham, a central plank of his work.
Crucially, as palace sources indicated, the King’s lack of involvement in the Invictus Games, which is very much the Duke’s project, should not be interpreted as a lack of approval.
When the event was launched in 2014, the King, then Prince Charles, joined his younger son at the opening ceremony, with the now Queen and Prince William.
Beyond that show of support, palace sources have previously insisted that senior members of the Royal family never involve themselves in each other’s work.
The Invictus Games and the Duke’s office have been approached for comment.
summary: Prince Harry and sources close to the Sussexes have blamed Uganda's withdrawal from the Invictus Games on a recent letter from Buckingham Palace. The letter, issued on the direction of the King, clarified that the Duke and Duchess are private citizens whose work is not on behalf of the monarchy. Ugandan military chief Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba cited a lack of the King's approval as the reason for pulling the country out of the event.
key_points: Uganda withdrew from the Invictus Games, claiming the event lacked King Charles III's approval.
A source close to the Sussexes blamed the withdrawal on a palace letter stating the couple are private citizens.
The controversial letter was issued by the Lord Chamberlain on the direction of the King.
Uganda had only joined the Invictus Games as the 26th participating nation in July.

title: Drag Race UK: BBC drops Ru Paul show after eight series
author: Josh Parry
content:
![Michelle Visage, Graham Norton, Ru Paul and Alan Carr on the main stage of Ru Paul's Drag Race UK. Michelle is wearing a latext dress, graham a golden blazer, and ru is wearing a pink and red dress with red furry boots. Alan is wearing a pink shirt and a leopard print blazer, stage lights illuminate the background and everyone is smiling at the camera for a promotional image.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/716f/live/1b5de710-ac86-11f1-ab14-5b9069dc795d.jpg)
The show has been broadcast on the BBC for eight series
- Published
RuPaul's Drag Race UK is leaving the BBC after eight series, the broadcaster has confirmed.
A spokesperson for the channel said it was facing "very difficult choices" in the face of "significant financial pressures".
The show is currently broadcast on BBC Three and iPlayer. Future series - as well as its spin-off vs The World - will be broadcast on Wow Presents Plus, a streaming platform owned by the production company behind the show.
At its peak, the UK version of the international drag competition averaged at around 1.5 million viewers per episode.
A spokesperson for the BBC said it was "proud [...] of this groundbreaking show" and thanked "RuPaul, World of Wonder and everyone involved, both on and off screen".
Started in 2019, Drag Race UK brought British drag into mainstream entertainment in the UK, and has made household names of drag performers such as La Voix, Danny Beard, and Tia Kofi.
The show sees drag queens compete in a series of challenges to impress judges RuPaul, Michelle Visage, Graham Norton and Alan Carr, and often features big name celebrity guest judges.
It has become a staple of LGBTQ+ culture and has been praised for its portrayal of the distinct style of British drag.
The corporation is currently rolling out plans to make Â£500m of savings, with director-general Matt Brittin previously telling staff "the scale of savings requires tough choices".
A BBC spokesperson said: "As the BBC continues to navigate significant financial pressures and deliver the savings required of us, we have had to make some very difficult choices, none of which have been taken lightly."
Announcing the news on Instagram, Wow Presents Plus said a "new era" of Drag Race UK was on the way.
A new series, Drag Race UK All Stars, which sees previous fan favourites return to compete again, will premier in Autumn 2027 exclusively on Wow Presents Plus.
BBC News understands the current series of Drag Race UK, which launched in September 2026, will continue to air as normal on BBC Three and appear on iPlayer, and all existing series will continue to be available once the move is complete.
The BBC declined to comment on whether future series of other international versions of the show, including Drag Race Canada and Drag Race Down Under, would continue to air.
Earlier this year, the BBC announced it was dropping LGBTQ+ dating show I Kissed a Boy - which made history as the UK's first gay dating show - and I Kissed a Girl.
Jordan Burrow, a contestant on series two of I Kissed a Boy, said the decision was an example of "where we're at within the queer community".
The corporation said at the time that it was "exceptionally proud" of the shows but they had to make "difficult choices in light of our funding challenges".
summary: The BBC has confirmed that RuPaul's Drag Race UK is leaving the broadcaster after eight series due to significant financial pressures and required savings. Future series and the vs The World spin-off will move exclusively to the streaming platform Wow Presents Plus. The current series airing on BBC Three and iPlayer will continue as normal.
key_points: RuPaul's Drag Race UK is ending its run on the BBC after eight series.
The decision is part of the BBC's efforts to make £500 million in savings amidst financial pressures.
Future series and the vs The World spin-off will be broadcast on Wow Presents Plus.
A new Drag Race UK All Stars series will premiere exclusively on Wow Presents Plus in Autumn 2027.
The current series and all existing episodes will remain available on BBC Three and iPlayer.

title: Ruby Rose Accuses Noel Clarke of Predation After ‘Doctor Who’ Actor Slapped With U.K. Criminal Charges
author: Etan Vlessing
content:
![Ruby Rose](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/GettyImages-1419244069-H-2022.jpg?w=1296&h=730&crop=1) 
Orange Is the New Black star Ruby Rose has alleged Noel Clarke was a predator on the set of the SAS: Rise of the Black Swan conspiracy thriller that shot in 2020.
Her accusation came on the same day the Doctor Who star was criminally charged in the U.K. with sexual assault, voyeurism and exposure. The offenses, brought by London’s Metropolitan Police, are alleged to have taken place between 2007 and 2016 and relate to five women.
“Noel Clarke has been charged. Years ago he preyed on a woman who worked on our SAS film. I reported him. No one cared. I was told not to get involved. Nobody followed up. So many came forward, finally some justice,” Rose wrote in a Threads post on Wednesday.
Related Stories
![Noel Clarke in 2025](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/wp-content/themes/vip/pmc-hollywoodreporter-2021/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif) 
![Katy Perry and Dolly Parton perform during the 61st Grammy Awards at Staples Center in Los Angeles on February 10, 2019.](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/wp-content/themes/vip/pmc-hollywoodreporter-2021/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif) 
Rose played Grace Lewis and Clarke had the role of Major Bisset in the 2021 thriller that also starred Andy Serkis, Tom Hooper, Hannah John-Kamen and Sam Heughan. The criminal charges against Clarke come five years after a Guardian exposé published claims from 20 women accusing the British actor of groping, sexual misconduct and bullying, as well as sources alleging they were “sexually harassed or inappropriately” touched on the set of Doctor Who.
Voyeurism refers to when someone secretly watches, photographs or films another person without their consent for sexual gratification. Rose gave no details of specific allegations against Clarke in her Threads post.
Rose also made sexual assault claims against Katy Perry after a nightclub incident in Melbourne in 2010 that led to an investigation by Australian police. Representatives for Perry refuted the alleged claims of a sexual offense by Rose as “reckless lies.”
The Hollywood Reporter did not immediately hear back from reps for Rose about her separate allegations against Clarke on Wednesday.

Clarke's criminal charges follow a previous Guardian exposé containing misconduct allegations from multiple women, while Rose also separately made disputed sexual assault claims against Katy Perry.

Rose stated she previously reported Clarke's behavior regarding a crew member, but her report was dismissed.

title: Lister Hospital failures led to death of Richard Branson’s wife
author: Telegraph Reporters
content:
![Lady Branson died aged 80 on Nov 24 after suffering a pulmonary embolism](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/09/09/TELEMMGLPICT000450471971_17889751521000_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqrX8JxY5lBYOlqPRWf6fjE9s4EdKZrYoiC92eMiQSQsQ.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Lady Branson died aged 80 on Nov 24 after suffering a pulmonary embolism](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/09/09/TELEMMGLPICT000450471971_17889751521000_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqrX8JxY5lBYOlqPRWf6fjE9s4EdKZrYoiC92eMiQSQsQ.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
A private hospital’s failure to provide preventative medication contributed to the death of Sir Richard Branson’s wife, an inquest has concluded.
Lady Branson died aged 80 on Nov 24 last year after suffering a cardiac arrest at the Lister Hospital in Chelsea, west London. The hospital is owned and operated by HCA Healthcare.
Westminster coroner’s court heard that she died after suffering a pulmonary embolism, a sudden blockage in a lung artery, resulting from deep-vein thrombosis.
Lady Branson was admitted to the hospital on Nov 17, weeks after suffering fractures of the pelvis and the hip in a fall on Necker Island, the private retreat in the Caribbean where she married Sir Richard in 1989.
Fiona Wilcox, senior coroner for Inner West London, said Lady Branson did not receive prophylactic anticoagulants at the hospital despite a “very high risk of developing deep-vein thrombosis”.
Giving her conclusion, the coroner said: “I do find her death would have likely been prevented, and the lack of anticoagulation did cause or contribute to her death probably.”
![Lady Branson was admitted to hospital suffering the after-effects of a fall weeks earlier on Necker Island, where she married Sir Richard in 1989](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/09/09/TELEMMGLPICT000450475793_17889757161160_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqpuXOTUYGo02viMRsPPNsptT2b7DP7EkmwMxOpoK2Y7w.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Earlier on Wednesday, witness Dr George Adams, a consultant haematologist at North West London NHS Hospitals Trust, told the court that the drugs reduced the risk of a blood clot.
Asked by the coroner whether Lady Branson had been “appropriately treated”, he agreed that anticoagulant drugs “would probably have prevented her death”.
He added that failure to apply compression stockings to Lady Branson’s legs in the first 48 hours of her admission might have made “a small contribution to the death”.
In an email sent to the court, the couple’s daughter, Dr Holly Branson, said her mother had a history of blood clots dating back to 2010 and would not have refused anticoagulants were they offered.
“Had I been aware she was not receiving Enoxaparin injections, I would have been very concerned given her recent long haul travel and medical history,” she wrote.
Dr Branson said her mother had not been given the anti-clot stockings to wear for up to 48 hours after her admission to hospital.
“I noticed she was not wearing them and asked the nurses,” she said. “My impression from the doctors was that this was an oversight on their part.”
![Holly Branson, pictured with her parents and brother Sam in 2004](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/09/09/TELEMMGLPICT000450471955_17889760497800_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqDkcnVA1td-zUqWAgIi5iRPXOe-PrP1-nuFS8qH0aKEI.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Dr Basir Kunduzi, who was on duty at the Lister Hospital when Lady Branson was admitted was asked by the coroner whether he thought she should have been given anti-coagulant injections.
“I thought she should have been,” he told the court, as he accepted it was his responsibility to prescribe the drugs.
Asked to explain why he did not give the drugs, he said: “Since Lady Branson had a fall and had been mobilised since her fall, there was a risk of bleeding.”
He said he decided to delay prescribing anti-coagulants until he had organised a CT scan to ensure there was no bleeding, which the drugs could have worsened.
But he said the decision not to administer the anti-coagulants to Lady Branson would live with him for the rest of his life, adding: “I would like to express my deepest condolences to Lady Branson’s family.”
In a statement read at the inquest by the coroner earlier, family members described Lady Branson as a “deeply loved wife, mother, grandmother and friend” who was “known for her warmth, kindness and unwavering compassion for others”.
On Instagram, Sir Richard described his wife as the “most wonderful mum and grandmum”, writing: “She was my best friend, my rock, my guiding light, my world. Love you forever Joan x.”
summary: An inquest has concluded that failures at the Lister Hospital in Chelsea contributed to the death of Sir Richard Branson’s wife, Lady Branson, at the age of 80. Lady Branson died from a pulmonary embolism after suffering a cardiac arrest on November 24 last year. The senior coroner stated that her death would likely have been prevented if she had received prophylactic anticoagulants for her high risk of deep-vein thrombosis.
key_points: Lady Branson died at the Lister Hospital in Chelsea after suffering a pulmonary embolism.
A coroner concluded that her death would likely have been prevented with appropriate anticoagulant medication.
Witnesses and family noted she was not given preventative anticoagulants or compression stockings in the initial hours of her admission.
The duty doctor accepted responsibility for not prescribing the drugs due to concerns about bleeding risks following her recent fall.

title: Sinkhole at Malibu home reportedly owned by Nicolas Cage prompts evacuation
author: Anna Betts
content:
The city of Malibu, California, has ordered the evacuation of more than 30 properties after a large sinkhole opened on Tuesday.
Malibu officials declared a local emergency on Tuesday evening after a “large sinkhole” emerged near 31630 Sea Level Drive. The officials said the sinkhole was believed to have begun developing on Monday, and had grown to roughly 25-30ft deep and 30 by 60ft wide by Tuesday evening.
In an earlier update on Tuesday, officials said they were responding to the “collapse of a driveway” and a resulting gas leak, which had been reported at about 5.45am local time. The Los Angeles county sheriff’s department and Los Angeles county fire department closed the private road and identified the gas leak.
Actor Nicolas Cage is reportedly the owner of the home where the sinkhole formed. Cage purchased the home in 2024, the New York Times noted. A representative for Cage did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
“Conditions are continuing to be evaluated, and the full extent of the impacts is not yet known,” Malibu city officials said on Tuesday evening, warning that the sinkhole “poses imminent danger to the homes and residents along Sea Level Drive”.
By Tuesday evening, 31 properties were under an evacuation order. Officials said that seven homes had been red-tagged because of “hazardous conditions resulting from the sinkhole” while another 24 residences were red-tagged “due to the loss of safe vehicular access”. Sheriff’s deputies notified residents in person and a digital alert had been issued.
Gas service to the affected area was shut off by Tuesday evening and city officials warned that water service “may also be discontinued as conditions warrant”.
They also cautioned that “conditions are likely to worsen with forecasted high tides and rains”. Additionally, Post-tropical Cyclone Marie could continue to bring “increased rainfall and high surf” to the area.
The National Weather Service said on Tuesday that “swells generated by Marie will continue to affect portions of the coast of the Baja California Peninsula and southern California for the next couple of days”.
A coastal flood advisory had been in effect until 11pm local time on Tuesday, Malibu officials said. A temporary shelter was also established by the American Red Cross at Malibu high school.
City officials said that emergency personnel access “is severely constrained and may be impassable, due to the large portion of the road that has collapsed”. They said that as of Tuesday evening, the “intact portion of the roadway is too narrow to accommodate emergency response vehicles, including fire engines and other large apparatus, creating a substantial risk to public safety and emergency response capabilities”.
summary: A large sinkhole measuring up to 30 feet deep and 60 feet wide opened on Sea Level Drive in Malibu, California, prompting the city to declare a local emergency. Over 30 properties were placed under evacuation orders, and several homes were red-tagged due to hazardous conditions and a loss of safe vehicular access. The affected property is reportedly owned by actor Nicolas Cage, and emergency crews are monitoring the situation as severe weather and high tides threaten to worsen the damage.
key_points: A massive sinkhole emerged near 31630 Sea Level Drive, initially following a driveway collapse and gas leak.
The city of Malibu ordered the evacuation of more than 30 properties, red-tagging several homes for safety hazards and blocked access.
Actor Nicolas Cage is reportedly the owner of the home where the sinkhole formed.
Gas service was shut off, and officials warned that conditions could worsen due to forecasted high tides, rains, and swells from Post-tropical Cyclone Marie.

title: Palace fears Sussexes building 'rival court' as war of words erupts
author: Richard Palmer
content:
King Charles’s efforts to clarify that the Duke and Duchess of Sussex should not be treated as royalty have led to a war of words between the two camps.
It comes amid palace concern – according to some royal insiders and commentators – over the growth of a rival Sussex court.
Such a court, insiders suggest, could have a potential to sow confusion now the Harry and Meghan are back in Britain, and planning charity engagements and commercial activities.
Shorts
The Sussexes were said to be frustrated that they received only an hour’s notice of a letter sent on behalf of the Palace on Monday to senior Government officials, the military and Lord-Lieutenants.
The letter stressed that the couple remain private individuals who should not be afforded the same privileges as working members of the Royal Family.
The couple are also said to object to being described as “private citizens” at all. Sources close to the Sussexes told The Telegraph they prefer the term “public figures”, and would have liked an acknowledgement that, on a personal level, they remain members of the Royal Family.
Palace officials, however, are understood to take the view that there was no need to consult them, as the document, as far as they are concerned, simply reaffirmed the position that has existed since the couple quit official royal duties in 2020.
They have declined to comment on the suggestion that the letter was prompted by concern over the couple creating a rival court.
Meanwhile. Harry and Meghan are worried that emphasising their status as private individuals could undermine their efforts to obtain armed police protection. The letter was sent as members of Ravec, the committee that advises the Home Office on protective security, prepared to meet this week to discuss their plea to have taxpayer-funded security while in the UK.
‘Weariness inside Buckingham Palace’
The whole episode, met with weariness inside Buckingham Palace, has soured what looked like an attempt at bridge-building by the Sussexes. It has revived memories of the rival press briefings that marked “Megxit“, and even carries echoes of the “War of the Waleses” in the 90s.
A third court – in the shape of the Prince and Princess of Wales’s office – adds to the complexities. William and Kate were more focused on Prince George’s first day at Eton on Monday, and have so far refused to discuss the Sussexes’s return. They are reportedly reluctant to reconcile or get involved in the drama.
While they are not thought to have been directly involved in drafting the letter, they are said to be “in lockstep” with the King who is keen to show his support for them, according to Kensington Palace officials.
A source close to the Sussexes insisted the couple want to rebuild familial relationships away from the cameras. While there is no prospect of them resuming official engagements, there remains the possibility that they could eventually be invited to public family gatherings such as Christmas at Sandringham, Easter at Windsor Castle, summer at Balmoral – as well as semi-official events such as Royal Ascot.
For the moment, at least, that is not on the cards. “They may see the family privately but I don’t think there are plans for them to get involved with public events with the institution,” the source noted, adding that they are not expected to join their relatives at Sandringham this Christmas.
“I think they have plans to spend it with family but other family.”
![Prince Harry, and Meghan, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, arrive for an event, during a visit to Bondi Beach, Australia, April 17, 2026. (Jonathan Brady/Pool Photo via AP, File)](https://inews.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/SEI_309555986.jpg?w=644)
It is not clear if that will be in Britain or in the US, where Meghan’s mother, Doria Ragland, is living in Los Angeles. Seeing the family of Harry’s mother – Diana, Princess of Wales – is also a priority for the couple.
In the coming weeks, their focus will be on settling their children into a new school, the location of which they have not confirmed.
The Prince has a series of charity engagements, including the WellChild Awards later in the month, a charity sky dive, and events connected to next summer’s Invictus Games in Birmingham.
Meghan ‘still in talks over Guy Ritchie role’
From their new UK base, the Duchess will work on her As Ever range of lifestyle products. There is talk of her resuming work for UK charities she previously represented, and she is also understood to still be in talks over a return to acting with a potential part in Guy Ritchie’s Netflix crime drama The Gentlemen.
However, the couple’s TV company, Archewell Productions, and their charitable operation, Archewell Philanthropies, will continue to be based in California, where they have kept their £11m home, along with a holiday home in Portugal, allowing for transatlantic trips and a potential exit.
The prospect of acting work for Meghan was one of several factors that led the couple to plan a return to Britain, as was educating their children, Prince Archie, seven, and Princess Lilibet, five, in the UK. “Now is a good time for them with Lily, as she says, going to big girls’ school. She’s gone into Year 1,” the source said.
But that does not mean they are here indefinitely. “The reason they are here isn’t down to one factor, similarly there will be a number of factors when – or if – they decide to move on,” the source said, adding that their relationship with the Royal Family was unlikely “to influence where they want to live”.
Inside the Royal Household, officials have suggested that the King wants to hold to the Sandringham agreement of 2020 under which the late Queen – backed by Charles and Prince William – ruled that the Sussexes could not be “half-in and half-out”, undertaking royal duties while making money commercially.
Some commentators, however, have suggested he may have to strip the couple of their royal titles to force them not to use them, to make the distinction between working and non-working royals clearer.
“It’s all they’ve got but I think Prince Harry ought to be worried about how easily Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor had his titles removed,” the royal biographer Hugo Vickers said. “It may have to happen if it gets really bad.”
summary: Tensions have arisen between Buckingham Palace and the Duke and Duchess of Sussex following a palace letter clarifying that the couple are private individuals without royal privileges. The Sussexes reportedly objected to the label, preferring to be called public figures, while insiders expressed concern over the growth of a rival Sussex court as the couple plans UK charity and commercial activities. The timing of the letter also coincided with discussions regarding their armed police protection in the UK.

title: Alan Carr holds back tears on special night at National Television Awards
author: Lola Schroer
content:
![Alan Carr accepts the 'Special Recognition' award on stage during the National Television Awards 2026 show at The O2 Arena.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/940/cpsprodpb/a316/live/f1f0d5f0-ac11-11f1-940e-bf738e043799.png)
The comedian was surprised with a top NTA honour
- Published
- You can see a full list of winners at the bottom of this article
Alan Carr had an emotional night at the 31st National Television Awards on Tuesday as he received the Special Recognition prize following a whirlwind year for the comedian.
The London audience had just been treated to a Traitors-themed musical performance in his honour, which included fellow cast member Paloma Faith emerging from a coffin, when he was given the surprise award.
Speaking to BBC News on the red carpet before the ceremony, Carr had played down his chances of winning for his semi-autobiographical comedy Changing Ends.
He joked: "Comedy is so subjective... Mrs Brown's Boys wins every year, why am I even here?"
Watch: 'I still felt bad about Paloma', says Alan Carr
Carr was right - Mrs Brown's Boys went on to win the Comedy prize. But the night was just beginning.
The Celebrity Traitors favourite had predicted there would be "ugly crying" if he did take home a prize - and he stayed true to his word as he accepted the Special Recognition award, the only category not voted for by the public.
Carr told BBC News that being part of The Celebrity Traitors had brought him a level of attention he had never experienced before.
"I've never had popularity like it," he said, describing the show as a "phenomenon".
![The cast of âThe Celebrity Traitorsâ accept the âReality Competitionâ Award onstage during the National Television Awards 2026 show at The O2 Arena](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/946/cpsprodpb/3887/live/b277eec0-ac0e-11f1-940e-bf738e043799.png)
The Celebrity Traitors won an award after a critically-acclaimed series
Carr had more reason to celebrate when The Celebrity Traitors beat the original version of the show to win the Reality Competition prize.
His co-star, singer Charlotte Church, praised the show's final, which attracted 15 million viewers within seven days, describing it as a "beautiful vignette of male tenderness and emotional expression".
"Alan, Nick (Mohammed) and David (Olusoga), you were just absolutely sublime," she added.
Sir David Attenborough wins an NTA at 100
Another big win went to Sir David Attenborough, who was named Best Presenter in his 100th birthday year, beating popular duo Ant and Dec, whose 23-year winning streak was broken by Gary Lineker last year.
While not in attendance, Attenborough's long-time collaborator Mark Brownlow accepted the award on his behalf and shared a message from the broadcaster urging people to help protect the planet.
"Humanity has always needed the natural world for all the practicalities of life and for our mental wellbeing," Attenborough wrote. "Now the natural world needs us too: surely we must not ignore that simple fact."
Clarkson's Farm wins again
Clarkson's Farm won an NTA for the second year running, taking the inaugural Celebrity-Led Reality Docuseries award.
The new category also featured shows from Stacey Solomon and Joe Swash, Tyson Fury, Kelvin Fletcher, and Bob Mortimer and Paul Whitehouse.
Celebrity-led programmes still featured in the Authored Documentary category, with documentaries from Olympian Sir Chris Hoy, former Little Mix singer Jesy Nelson, and Sharon Osbourne's film about her late husband Ozzy among the nominees.
![Jeremy Clarkson holding an award in the air](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/999/cpsprodpb/d33b/live/35781610-abec-11f1-9367-3bcf2710718d.jpg)
It was a win for a second year in a row for Jeremy Clarkson
Speaking to BBC News on the red carpet, their daughter Kelly Osbourne said her family were "honoured" that the documentary about her father had been nominated, describing it as a "tragic but beautiful story".
She said she had spoken to her mother Sharon just before arriving at the ceremony: "We are so close. I was on the phone with her before I got out of the car."
In the end, the public chose Our Girls: The Southport Families. The BBC programme followed the families of Alice da Silva Aguiar, nine, Bebe King, six, and Elsie Dot Stancombe, seven, who were murdered at a Taylor Swift-themed dance class in Southport in 2024.
Accepting the award, Elsie's mother Jenni Stancombe told the audience: "We never expected to be stood up here, so I don't know what to say.
"We know you didn't vote for us, you voted for our three girls."
![Jenni Stancombe accepts the âAuthored Documentaryâ Award for âOur Girls: The Southport Familiesâ onstage at the National Television Awards](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/937/cpsprodpb/9773/live/694952e0-ac20-11f1-9bd9-7b7da208bd5c.png)
The parents of the Southport attack victims were recognised for their powerful film documenting the lives of their daughters
'We are dominating that category'
In the drama categories, Vicky McClure won Best Drama Performance for her role in crime thriller Trigger Point, from the first all-female shortlist in the category's history.
She told BBC News in the winners' room: "Over the years it has not been our space, and here we are dominating that category.
"I feel honoured to be amongst those wonderful women."
![Vicky McClure holding an award](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/999/cpsprodpb/5521/live/6b9cdd70-abec-11f1-9367-3bcf2710718d.jpg)
Vicky McClure came out on top in a list of nominees dominated by female actors
Among those nominated alongside McClure was Sheridan Smith for her portrayal of campaigner Ann Ming in ITV true crime drama I Fought The Law.
While Smith missed out on the individual prize, I Fought The Law went on to win New Drama.
Norton dusts off his Swift-Kelce wedding suit
Away from the awards, nominee Graham Norton revealed his red carpet outfit had already had one high-profile outing this year.
"This is what I wore to Taylor Swift's wedding," he told BBC News.
Norton said guests had agreed not to reveal details of the celebrations. "I had a wonderful time and we all agreed by saying yes to going, we weren't going to blab about it."
Norton, who also featured in Swift's music video for Opalite earlier this year, said working with the singer showed him "what leadership is like at that level".
"It was such a happy set. Everyone was working as hard as they could for her," he said.
![Graham Norton smiles as he stands on the National Television Awards red carpet](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1800/cpsprodpb/98ca/live/7f0e1030-abe3-11f1-bce3-af8c1549772d.jpg)

title: How meteorologists recreated weather that helped decide second world war
author: Nicola Davis
content:
Dressed in a Royal Air Force uniform and sporting a trim moustache, Andrew Scott looks slightly queasy – as well he might. Behind him is a huge map of the Channel, and in front of him is Brendan Fraser, looming with a request: “I need a forecast,” he says.
Starring in the film Pressure, based on a true story, Scott plays the meteorologist Gp Capt James Stagg – the man who must tell Gen Eisenhower – played by Fraser – whether conditions will be suitable for the D-day landings scheduled to take place on 5 June 1944. But a large storm is approaching the Normandy coast.
The film, showing in cinemas in the UK and Ireland from 9 September, unites two topics that ceaselessly fascinate the British: the second world war – and weather.
It is also a rare treat for meteorologists, who are not hugely represented on the big screen and are delighted to be portrayed as the heroes of a film.
Dr Stephen Burt of the University of Reading, an adviser for the film, said the challenge Stagg and his colleagues faced was enormous. “To do a forecast beyond 24 hours was, in the 1940s, like trying to land a man on the moon,” he said.
Scientists had only recently started to use upper air data to predict the weather, he said, and largely relied on surface measurements of pressure, temperature, dew point, wind speed and direction, and experience-based intuition.
One difficulty is that most of our weather comes in from the Atlantic. “Nowadays we have satellites and so on and we can see what’s coming, we have observations coming from the US,” he said. “But then there were … just a couple of ships, a couple of submarines maybe and some aircraft observations. And that’s it.”
Crucially, the week before D-day was the hottest May week on record, Burt said – a high that was only broken this year. Then a huge storm blew up, with another close behind.
![British troops take positions on Sword beach during D-day on 6 June 1944.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/88fd6ec30df6d0b67d494729853baebe28d02b5e/0_0_3500_2472/master/3500.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Prof Ed Hawkins of the University of Reading, an expert in historical weather data collection and examination, including D-day, explains that there were three teams working on the D-day forecasts – although only two are depicted in the film – all feeding into Stagg. But they took different approaches and produced different forecasts.
It was up to Stagg to reconcile the results and present a recommendation to Eisenhower that would, ultimately, affect 160,000 Allied troops. “Stagg was in a very difficult position. He left his very pregnant wife to come and do this very important task,” Hawkins said.
The teams were split about the forecast for 5 June – with Stagg concluding the conditions would be too perilous. The landings were postponed. But by the evening of 4 June a consensus emerged: there appeared to be a small but suitable window on 6 June. The invasion was back on.
“They managed to do the forecast, and the invasion, and get away with it,” said Burt.
Burt and his colleagues agree that even modern systems based on artificial intelligence have struggled to accurately predict conditions for 6 June 1944 using data available from the time.
“[I’d] still have been chewing my fingernails on morning of the sixth,” said Burt.
Catherine Ross, a Met Office archivist, said film-makers used exact replicas of records from June 1944. “We were able to provide images of every single weather chart that was being produced at the time. We had codes and examples of how the observations were sent in and all sorts of documentation,” she said.
She notes that even before modern technology, allied forecasters were on the front foot in terms of access to data. They already had data from the UK and across the Atlantic. “But because of Bletchley Park they had broken the Enigma code, so they had access to all of the German weather observations as well,” Ross said.
While the German forces may have been aware of the storms, they were not aware of a potential break in the weather. “Sometimes there’s no Atlantic on the [German] chart, which is where the weather was coming from in early June 1944,” she added.
It is no spoiler that D-day was a success for the British, but the film sheds new light on the drama that unfolded behind the scenes.
“It’s the most famous forecast ever made by the Met Office. It’s probably one of the most important weather forecasts in history,” said Ross.
summary: The upcoming film Pressure depicts the true story of Royal Air Force meteorologist Gp Capt James Stagg, who advised Gen Eisenhower on the weather conditions for the D-day landings in June 1944. Relying on limited data from the Atlantic, surface measurements, and intercepted German observations via Bletchley Park, Stagg successfully persuaded Eisenhower to postpone the invasion due to a severe storm and identify a narrow window of suitable weather for 6 June. Meteorological advisers and archivists assisted the filmmakers by providing exact replicas of historical weather charts and documentation from the era.
key_points: Andrew Scott stars as meteorologist James Stagg and Brendan Fraser as Gen Eisenhower in the film Pressure, opening in UK and Ireland cinemas on 9 September.
In the 1940s, forecasting beyond 24 hours was extremely difficult, relying on surface measurements, intuition, and scarce data from the Atlantic.
Stagg had to reconcile differing forecasts from multiple teams and ultimately advised Eisenhower to postpone the D-day landings from 5 June to 6 June.
Allied forecasters had an advantage because Bletchley Park broke the Enigma code, giving them access to German weather observations while German forces lacked Atlantic data.
