title: Monty Don to leave Gardeners' World after more than 20 years
author: Steven McIntosh
content:
![Monty Don pictured on Gardeners' World in 2024](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/36c9/live/5d567720-ab7f-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.jpg)
- Published
Monty Don is to step down as the host of Gardeners' World after more than 20 years, the BBC has announced.
The 71-year-old, who is the programme's longest-serving head gardener, will leave at the end of the current series.
In a statement, Don said working on the show had been a "deeply rewarding experience," but added: "Now is the right time for a change."
The BBC said Don had "inspired and guided millions of viewers with his warmth, wisdom and passion for gardening" since joining the programme in 2003.
Don began presenting the programme at Berryfields, a rented garden in Stratford-upon-Avon, before it moved in 2011 to his own garden, Longmeadow in Herefordshire.
"Throughout that time - and around 700 programmes - I have had the privilege of sharing my own abiding passion for gardens and gardening with an equally passionate, and often equally knowledgeable audience," he said.
"That connection with millions, not just in Britain but across the world, who share a love of gardens, plants and the natural world is something I have always treasured and which I increasingly believe to be at the heart of a life well lived."
Don added he had "always relished the craft of programme making" and paid tribute to the "superlative BBC team" he worked with over the years.
"I look forward to continuing to work with and for the BBC on other projects, as well as following new avenues," he concluded. "And of course, I will still be gardening, dog by side, here at Longmeadow."
'A nation of budding gardeners'
The presenter, whose full name is George Montague Don, made his TV debut in 1989 with a gardening segment on ITV's This Morning.
That led to further work on the BBC and Channel 4, a newspaper column, and the publication of more than 20 books about gardening authored by Don.
He replaced Alan Titchmarsh on Gardeners' World in 2003, but took a break from the programme in 2008 as he recovered from a stroke.
He has also presented other programmes including Around the World in 80 Gardens, My Dream Farm, Mastercrafts, Monty Don's Rhineland Gardens, and coverage of the Chelsea Flower Show.
The BBC's chief content officer Kate Phillips described Don as "unique", adding he was "a wonderfully engaging broadcaster with a soothing, calm presence who has inspired so many".
"Monty's decision to leave Gardeners' World is one I respect, but I'm still very sad he's leaving," she added.
"We are a nation full of budding gardeners, and his tips and advice have been invaluable to viewers for more than 20 years and have certainly helped me increase my knowledge as well as my plant survival rate!
"I would like to thank Monty personally for his honesty and kindness which has seen him open up about his own personal struggles and the power of the natural world to improve mental health. We will miss him on the show hugely."
Don has been open about his struggle with depression over the years.
summary: Monty Don is stepping down as the host of Gardeners' World after more than 20 years, with his departure set for the end of the current series. The BBC's longest-serving head gardener began hosting the show in 2003 and filmed approximately 700 programmes. Don stated that while working on the show was rewarding, now is the right time for a change, though he plans to continue working with the BBC on other projects.
key_points: Monty Don is leaving Gardeners' World at the end of the current series after more than 20 years as host.
He has been the programme's longest-serving head gardener since joining in 2003 and filmed about 700 programmes.
Don plans to continue working with the BBC on other projects and will keep gardening at his Longmeadow home.
The BBC praised Don for inspiring millions of viewers and for his openness about mental health and the natural world.

title: Renoir paintings worth millions stolen in French museum heist
author: Michael Sheils McNamee; Tiffany Wertheimer
content:
What we know about the Renoir museum heist
- Published
Two paintings by the impressionist artist Pierre-Auguste Renoir have been stolen from a museum in the south of France.
Two thieves broke into the Renoir Museum in Cagnes-sur-Mer early on Tuesday, seizing four paintings but dropping two of the works in the museum gardens as they escaped, local Mayor Bryan Masson said.
The paintings, each worth â¬9m (Â£7.7m; $10.4m), are the latest high-profile pieces to have been stolen in a string of recent heists in Europe which have thrust the security of art in galleries and museums into the spotlight.
One of the most high-profile was in October last year, when a brazen heist at the Louvre Museum in Paris saw France's priceless crown jewels being stolen.
CCTV footage captured the thieves entering the Renoir museum gardens by cutting through a fence before they cut through structures holding the paintings' frames in place, the local mayor said.
The alarm went off at 05:48 (05:48 GMT), and police were at the scene within five minutes, Masson explained, saying the thieves fled the scene upon hearing the security alarms.
He later told reporters that the thieves seemed to be "well-equipped" and "well-informed".
They were "wearing helmets, gloves, and combat gear" and carrying "an electric knife and hacksaw," he added.
Investigators have found two zip-up bags at the scene, which may have belonged to the suspects.
![A composite image of the two paintings which are in gold frames.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1600/cpsprodpb/2637/live/3d9d95d0-ab7f-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.jpg)
Jeune fille au puits and Portrait of Madame Colonna Romano are still missing
The mayor said that two paintings were "abandoned" in the gardens and have now been recovered.
The two paintings that are still missing are:
- Portrait of Madame Colonna Romano (1910)
- Jeune fille au puits (1886)
And the two pieces that were recovered are:
- Portrait of Madame Pichon (1895)
- Coco Lisant (1905)
"Attacking the Renoir Museum is attacking a part of the history and heritage of Cagnes-sur-Mer," the mayor told reporters at the museum.
"It's Renoir's, it is priceless, you cannot sell it like that," he said.
![A composite image of the two paintings which are in gold frames.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1600/cpsprodpb/fd0c/live/42f33f30-ab7f-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.jpg)
The thieves dropped Coco Lisant and Portrait of Madame Pichon when they fled - one was found hours later in the museum's garden
The Renoir Museum is home to 12 of the famous painter's artworks.
Opened in 1960, it was Renoir's last home before his death in 1919, and also features many things that once belonged to him, including his easel and wheelchair, as well as photographs and personal letters.
Last month, four Renaissance paintings were stolen from a museum in Sicily.
"Beyond Cagnes-sur-Mer, this incident should serve as a warning about the protection of our museums, which now face a new form of organised crime targeting works of art," the local French mayor warned.
Masson called on the French government to provide more financial support to local areas and museums to protect artwork from "increasingly organised and determined criminals".
![Annotated aerial map of the Renoir museum estate in in Cagnes-sur-Mer, France. The museum building, gardens and main entrance are labelled within a white outline marking the property boundary. A red label indicates the location where a hole was cut in the perimeter fence on the western side of the grounds, near AllÃ©e Victor Vasarely. An inset map of France shows the site in the south-east of the country.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1600/cpsprodpb/7a6b/live/913ea0b0-ab9a-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.jpg)
summary: Two Pierre-Auguste Renoir paintings were stolen during a museum heist in Cagnes-sur-Mer, France, while two other works were dropped in the gardens and recovered. The well-equipped thieves cut through a fence and security structures before fleeing when the alarm sounded. Each of the stolen artworks is valued at millions of euros, highlighting ongoing security concerns for European museums.
key_points: Two thieves broke into the Renoir Museum in Cagnes-sur-Mer early on Tuesday.
Four paintings were initially seized, but two were abandoned in the museum gardens and later recovered.
The two missing paintings are Portrait of Madame Colonna Romano and Jeune fille au puits, each valued at 9 million euros.
Police arrived at the scene within five minutes of the alarm sounding, causing the suspects to flee.
The local mayor described the suspects as well-equipped and well-informed, wearing combat gear and carrying tools like an electric knife and hacksaw.

title: Harry and Meghan ‘surprised’ at king’s letter reiterating they are non-working royals
author: Caroline Davies
content:
The Duke and Duchess of Sussex were “surprised” at being given little notice of a formal letter sent to government departments and the military on behalf of King Charles reiterating their status as non-working royals.
Harry and Meghan, who returned to the UK from the US two weeks ago, had insufficient time to clarify any points before details were issued to the media, it is understood.
The letter, the first official public clarification of the couple’s status since their return, was issued by Buckingham Palace’s most senior officer, the lord chamberlain, Richard Benyon.
It was revealed to the media at 3.06pm on Monday. It is understood the contents were shared with Harry and Meghan’s team almost an hour before at 1.59pm, who sent a response back to Buckingham Palace at 2.19pm asking whether the guidance had already gone out, in the hope of letting the couple know before the media, and for the team to have the chance to clarify one or two points.
Harry was in a meeting and could not be contacted until 3.09pm. The Sussexes’ team received confirmation at 3.11pm it had already been sent to the media.
The letter was revealed before a reported meeting this week of the executive committee for the protection of royalty and public figures (Ravec), which is responsible for making decisions about royal security.
Harry is waiting to hear the conclusion of the risk management board’s threat assessment and Ravec is expected to decide at the meeting whether the Sussexes are entitled to taxpayer-funded security now they live in the UK. The Home Office does not comment on such decision making and would be unlikely to reveal the outcome of such a meeting.
Lord Benyon’s letter reiterates the couple’s “current” status as non-working royals. “This position, distinct from the state and royal duties undertaken by the working royal family, and with the personal latitude it brings the couple in respect of financial independence and protection of their privacy as they would wish, will continue to be fully respected.
“Their styles as His and Her Royal Highness remain in abeyance and are not used.
It says their charitable work “is a personal matter for them both and undertaken in their private capacity”.
“In short, their position is akin to private citizens with commercial and charitable interests.”
The letter says questions from official and state organisations about the courtesies extended to the couple, “and particularly where recourse to public funds may be required”, should be directed to Buckingham Palace, adding: “Any operational security issues should continue to be directed to the relevant police authorities.”
The couple’s children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, are expected to be starting school in the UK near to the family’s reported countryside retreat.
The palace’s clarification came on the day Harry was revealed to have visited Tower Bridge Studios, a London filming and podcast studio, where shows such as the podcasts Diary of a CEO and Jimmy Carr’s The Big Pitch are recorded.
summary: The Duke and Duchess of Sussex were reportedly surprised after receiving short notice about a formal letter from Buckingham Palace that reiterated their status as non-working royals. Sent by the lord chamberlain to government departments and the military, the letter was shared with the couple's team shortly before being released to the media. The clarification comes ahead of a reported meeting regarding taxpayer-funded security for the family, who recently returned to the UK.
key_points: Harry and Meghan had insufficient time to clarify points before a formal letter regarding their non-working royal status was released to the media.
The letter was issued by Richard Benyon, the lord chamberlain, to government departments and the military.
The guidance states that the couple's position is akin to private citizens with commercial and charitable interests, with their HRH styles remaining in abeyance.
The letter preceded a reported meeting of the executive committee for the protection of royalty and public figures (Ravec) regarding security.
The couple's children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, are expected to start school in the UK.

title: Prince George arrives at Eton, the elite school that taught his father and 20 UK prime ministers | CNN
author: Lauren Said-Moorhouse
content:
Britain’s Prince George has started the next stage of his education with his first day at Eton College on Tuesday.
The 13-year-old is following in the footsteps of his father Prince William and his uncle, Prince Harry - both of whom attended the prestigious school outside of London.
George appeared to be in good spirits despite the gloomy fall weather as he made his way to his new school accompanied by his parents, William and Catherine.
George, who is second in line to the British throne, arrived in a jacket, shirt and tie and dark trousers but will likely soon have to change into the school’s uniform of a black tailcoat, waistcoat and pinstriped trousers, with a stiff white collar.
The family crossed the historic institution’s School Yard, a cobblestoned quad with a statue of King Henry VI, who founded the school in 1440, at its center before being met by the school’s principal Simon Henderson and provost Nicholas Coleridge.
The group chatted for a few minutes, with Henderson heard telling his new student: “Welcome, good luck, enjoy it.”
![William, Catherine and George are met by Eton principal Simon Henderson, second left, and provost Nicholas Coleridge, left, on their arrival.](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/gettyimages-2293659463.jpg?c=original&q=w_860,c_fill)
![Eton College is a short distance from the Wales' family home of Forest Lodge in Windsor Great Park. (Photo by Adrian DENNIS / POOL / AFP via Getty Images)](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/gettyimages-2293661216.jpg?c=original&q=w_860,c_fill)
Eton College, located in the English county of Berkshire a stone’s throw from Windsor Castle, educates boys aged 13 to 18 and accepts around 270 students per academic year. Students live on campus in its 25 dormitories. Each boarding house has around 55 students and is led by a house master.
Prince William attended the school from 1995, while Prince Harry did so from 1998.
It is one of Britain’s most famous and prestigious fee-paying schools, with a notable list of alumni that also includes celebrities and 20 of the country’s 59 prime ministers.
Former Conservative prime ministers Boris Johnson, who led the UK from 2019 to 2022, and David Cameron, who was in office from 2010 to 2016, are both former students.
Other famous Old Etonians include actors Hugh Laurie, Tom Hiddleston and Eddie Redmayne.
The school fees for the current 2025/26 year at Eton is £63,298.80 (about $84,900).
Prior to starting at Eton, George attended Lambrook School, a private prep school near Windsor, alongside his siblings, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis.
CNN’s Jack Guy contributed to this story.
summary: Britain's Prince George has started his first day at Eton College, accompanied by his parents, Prince William and Catherine. The 13-year-old is second in line to the British throne and follows in the footsteps of his father and uncle, who also attended the prestigious boarding school. Upon arrival, the family was greeted by the school's principal and provost.
key_points: Prince George began his education at Eton College on Tuesday.
He was accompanied to the school by his parents, Prince William and Catherine.
Eton College is a prestigious, fee-paying boarding school for boys aged 13 to 18.
Prince William and Prince Harry both previously attended Eton College.
Before attending Eton, George was a student at Lambrook School.

title: Gary Oldman says new James Bond has been decided
author: Lauren Hunter
content:
![Gary Oldman - James Bond - Split - 2026](https://cdn1.faroutmagazine.co.uk/uploads/1/2026/09/Gary-Oldman-James-Bond-Split-2026-Far-Out-Magazine-1140x855.jpg)
Gary Oldman claims the new James Bond has been cast: “They have picked him”
Although having no previous involvement in the franchise, Gary Oldman has claimed that the next James Bond has been cast.
One of the most coveted roles in cinema has been up for grabs ever since Daniel Craig stepped back from playing the world’s most famous spy following the release of No Time To Die in 2021.
With names such as Callum Turner, Aaron Taylor-Johnson, and Jacob Elordi all reportedly in contention, Oldman has now seemingly thrown another actor in the ring, in the form of his Slow Horses co-star Jack Lowden.
Speaking of the prospect of the Scottish actor playing Bond in an interview with Global News in Canada, Oldman said: “It’s been rumored that he’s on the shortlist. We’re going to find out pretty soon, aren’t we?”, per Deadline.
However, the actor’s comments turned the most heads when he added, “Because they have picked him. They have made their choice, but they have not announced it yet. So my fingers are crossed for Jack.”
Whether Oldman has inadvertently let slip that Lowden has been cast in the role remains to be seen, but it comes with the understanding that an official announcement could be made in the coming months.
This was confirmed by the film’s producer, Amy Pascal, who said in an interview with Deadline in August that “the end of the year is a good bet” for when the casting will be revealed.
The future of the James Bond franchise has been kept strictly under wraps ever since Amazon MGM Studios took over creative control of the series from the Broccoli family last year.
The studio previously released a statement in May to say that the casting process was underway, though they have not yet made any public response to Oldman’s comments over Lowden.
There is the possibility that the creative team could be waiting for director Denis Villeneuve’s latest film, Dune: Part Three, to be released in cinemas on December 19th before they make any moves.

summary: Actor Gary Oldman has claimed that the next James Bond has already been chosen, though an official announcement has not yet been made. Oldman expressed hope that his Slow Horses co-star, Jack Lowden, who is rumored to be on the shortlist, is the one who got the role. The James Bond franchise has been under the creative control of Amazon MGM Studios since last year, with producer Amy Pascal suggesting an announcement could come by the end of the year.
key_points: Gary Oldman claims the next James Bond actor has been chosen but not yet announced.
Oldman hopes his Slow Horses co-star Jack Lowden has secured the role.
Producer Amy Pascal previously indicated that a casting announcement could happen by the end of the year.
Amazon MGM Studios took over creative control of the franchise from the Broccoli family last year.

title: 20 Incredible Modern Horror Movies That Came Out Of NOWHERE
author: Jordan Blum
content:
![Obsession](https://d2thvodm3xyo6j.cloudfront.net/media/2026/09/492e9be0b8a75e355beb295f4e986ee3-600x338.jpg) 
Over the past few years, there've been plenty of horror releases from established filmmakers and franchises that were on genre lovers’ radars.
For example, and regardless of whether they're good or bad, you can’t honestly say that the newest Scream, Evil Dead, Hellraiser, Halloween, Insidious, and Terrifier sequels didn't arrive without plenty of attention. Likewise, you couldn’t seriously argue that Trap, Beau is Afraid, Nosferatu, and Thanksgiving came from unknown names.
However, many of the greatest recent horror pictures snuck up on people, for one reason or another.
In some cases, they’re first-time efforts from burgeoning directors who obviously had no proven track record. Or, they marked the creative and commercial breakthroughs of visionaries who’d already done some solid but underappreciated work.
Elsewhere, these movies signified the introductions of known quantities in other genres – such as comedy – who tried their hands at something scary. Perhaps most impressively, they may be legacy sequels to long-dead franchises that were significantly better than they had any right to be.
Whatever the circumstances, the following films easily count as 20 incredible recent horror movies that came out of nowhere!
(As you might guess, spoilers ahead!)
20. Together
![Together](https://d2thvodm3xyo6j.cloudfront.net/media/2025/08/3b9494911d2dc7787ae9e8240b4e50cb-600x338.webp) 
Despite having some inherent appeal as a new entry in one of horror’s most beloved subgenres – body-horror – there were a few reasons to be skeptical about 2025’s Together.
Primarily, main stars and actual married couple Alison Brie and Dave Franco were known for their comedic chops and occasional dramatic leanings, so the fact that they’ve barely done any scary cinema beforehand could’ve been a red flag. Likewise, Together was the feature-length debut of writer/director Michael Shanks, meaning that it was being helmed by someone largely unknown and unproven.
Nevertheless, Together was met with widespread acclaim and respectable financial profits.
Unsurprisingly, Brie and Franco were great as Millie and Tim, respectively, effortlessly mixing their real-life chemistry with the fictionalized complications of their characters. In particular, Together did a fantastic job of complementing its superficial weirdness and violence with thoughtful subtext regarding failed ambitions, co-dependency, and the all-too-relatable romantic dilemma of staying with someone out of complacency rather than true compatibility.
Plus, it harkened back to the bizarreness, discomfort, and mystery of the best body-horror pictures from decades past, with superbly off-putting effects, designs, and situations making audiences squirm throughout the runtime.
Fortunately, Together stuck the landing, too, with a resolution that’s simultaneously grotesque, logical, and unforgettable.
summary: While many recent horror movies come from established franchises and well-known filmmakers, others surprise audiences by sneaking up out of nowhere. A prime example is the 2025 body-horror film Together, directed by feature-length debutant Michael Shanks and starring comedic actors Alison Brie and Dave Franco. Despite initial skepticism, the movie received widespread acclaim and financial success for blending grotesque effects with thoughtful subtext about co-dependency and failed ambitions.
key_points: Many recent horror films are surprise hits from first-time directors, genre-switching actors, or unexpected legacy sequels.
The 2025 movie Together is a body-horror film starring real-life married couple Alison Brie and Dave Franco.
Together marked the feature-length directorial debut of Michael Shanks.
The film was met with widespread acclaim and financial success, praised for both its off-putting effects and its subtext on co-dependency.

title: Colin from Accounts final season review – farewell to a blinding ray of TV sunshine
author: Rachel Aroesti
content:
There are cliffhangers, and then there’s whatever happened at the end of Colin from Accounts’ second season. We had, by that point, witnessed protagonists Ashley and Gordon’s unconventional love story evolve from bizarre meet-cute – key stages: boob-flashing, car accident, injured dog – to soulmate-level relationship. But what starts with an exposed nipple can abruptly go tits up. On a heaving dancefloor at Ash’s best friend’s wedding, Gordon – drunk and buoyed up by the DJ dropping Slice of Heaven by Dave Dobbyn (the Oceanian equivalent of Come on Eileen, judging by the euphoric reaction) – decides to ask his girlfriend to marry him. Ash, humiliated by the circumstances, doesn’t respond. Everyone else films it and laughs. Gordon insists the whole thing was a joke and awkwardly boogies on. Then the credits roll.
If you had somehow managed to wipe this eye-watering faux pas from your mind’s eye, fear not: the Aussie rom-sitcom returns for its third and final series by replaying the agonising proposal in full. It gets worse. We discover the pair split soon after and haven’t seen each other for three years. In fact, they’ve both since found other (extremely attractive) partners: the kind but dim David and the hyper-capable and efficient Chelsea. As Ash later observes, they’ve “upgraded” – but you know their respective hearts don’t really belong to their nice new beaux.
![Nice new beaux … Ashley (Harriet Dyer), and David (Thomas Coquerel) in Colin from Accounts.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/f318f5cd26a6b4bf664255b9aae6512f339a59f0/0_0_2994_2290/master/2994.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Colin from Accounts – which is also the name of the dog the pair maim then adopt at the start of the show – is the sort of sitcom that runs almost entirely on charm. After all, there is no other way to convince an audience to watch two people fall in love, split up, get back together, split up again, then (I assume – the final two episodes weren’t available for review) reunite once more aside from cultivating a deep and lasting affection for them. This, however, is a mysterious art. The fact the pair are played by real-life couple and show co-creators Patrick Brammall and Harriet Dyer provides a frisson of autobiographical intrigue and obviously helps with the chemistry, but it’s hard to pin down what exactly it is about these characters that is so appealing: they’re both annoying, immature and petty, and far from morally upstanding (once they bump into each other again, it’s not long before they’ve betrayed David and Chelsea). Still, we desperately want them to find love, ideally with each other.
Think of it like Friends if it had just been about Ross and Rachel, with the other characters consigned to supporting eccentrics. Among the roster of weirdos here is Ash’s stunningly awful mother Lynelle and her alarmingly creepy husband Lee, who are now deeply entrenched in the men’s rights movement. Then there’s Gordon’s thoroughly unreconstructed brother Heavy (catnip for Lynelle, then), plus his brewery colleagues – the furious yet resoundingly cool Chiara and hulking sweetheart Brett – alongside Ash’s bestie Megan and her wife Rumi. The fact that three of the last four turn out to be sex party people does later serve to make Ash and Gordon seem like relatable nerds in comparison.
You probably wouldn’t describe Colin from Accounts as a hard comedy: its primary objective is to make us invest in its central will-they-won’t-they, and therefore prioritises well-drawn friendships, realistic romantic messiness and amusingly sour banter over non-stop jokes. That said, it can be laugh-out-loud funny when it wants to be. This series seems to have saved all its best material for its third episode, which involves a particularly grim morning for Ashley, now a qualified GP, thanks to an old man who has brought in his stool diary and samples. Blessedly, she is forced to cut his appointment short when she discovers Lynelle has posted a video about her own murder on Facebook (“take your shit! Get up – go, mate!”). Later, when Ash and Gordon meet at a fancy restaurant to discuss their adulterous kiss at the latter’s birthday party, a smug waiter pours wine in excessively long, urine-like streams from a traditional Spanish pitcher in what feels like a reprise of classic 1990s sitcom silliness.
Ultimately, though, this is an immensely comforting show: very sweet, very gentle, yet prevented from tipping into saccharine territory by a bass note of blokey and invariably profane Australian humour. The insults are particularly impressive – it’s difficult to choose a favourite from this series but I think I’ll go with the simple but effective “fucking cockhead” (credit: Lynelle’s ex Bernie discussing her current husband Lee). Cringe comedy – and what feels like a slightly misjudged subplot about child abduction – aside, Colin from Accounts has been like a ray of sunshine in the schedules. It’s been a huge hit across the world, and many will mourn its ending. I hope it turns out to be a happy one at least.
summary: The Australian rom-sitcom "Colin from Accounts" returns for its third and final season, picking up three years after an awkward public proposal caused Ashley and Gordon to split. Despite both characters finding attractive new partners, their undeniable chemistry and the show's signature charm drive the narrative toward an expected reunion. Filled with a colorful cast of eccentric supporting characters and profane humor, the comforting series relies on romantic messiness and well-drawn relationships rather than non-stop jokes.
key_points: The third and final season begins three years after Gordon's disastrous, public marriage proposal to Ashley.
Following the breakup, both Ashley and Gordon acquired new partners before inevitably crossing paths again.
Real-life couple and co-creators Patrick Brammall and Harriet Dyer star as the flawed yet deeply appealing main characters.
The series features a robust roster of eccentric supporting characters, including Ashley's controversial mother Lynelle and Gordon's brewery colleagues.
The show prioritizes emotional investment, realistic romantic messiness, and sour banter over traditional non-stop jokes.

title: From a paediatric doctor to a podium dancer: meet the 2026 stars of The Great British Bake Off
author: Stuart Heritage
content:
The new contestants of this year’s Great British Bake Off don’t know how lucky they are. Usually when a new intake arrives, all eyes are on them. After all, this is a show with such a long and storied history that its audience is primed for the slightest culinary mistake.
But this time around the contestants will enjoy a temporary reprieve, because this is the year when Bake Off becomes The Nigella Show, and everyone will be so busy going moon-eyed over its glamorous new judge that they’ll barely even give the bakers a second look.
Nevertheless, as is tradition, Channel 4 has just sent out its contestant biographies. Using them, and no other quantifiable data, let’s rank their chances of success from worst to best, just for the hell of it.
Clara, 24, marketing graduate, Hertfordshire
![A blond woman holds a baked loaf of bread.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/8e2e34b83bbeb9db00df4b2cbc3f5dd830449ce4/0_93_2604_3036/master/2604.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Things aren’t looking great for Clara. A Portuguese “fantasy girlie”, it is said that her signature style is “chaotically beautiful”. As everybody knows, this is code for “Clara is not detail oriented”. What’s more, her official show biography states that she believes “the first bite of a bake is always with the eyes”. However, the first bite of anything is with the mouth. Eyes, by their very nature, cannot bite things. This failure to understand basic anatomy will almost certainly be her undoing.
Mo, 21, law student, West Midlands
![A young man with dark hair holds kitchen utensils in each hands are he crosses his arms.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/1846de11db0d3c93a62d7a0a82390e45dc2595fc/98_68_2332_2862/master/2332.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Again, everything about Mo sounds like a whopping great red flag. In his contestant questionnaire he professes to not owning any cookbooks, calls himself “chaotic and random”, declares that he enjoys “winging it” and admits that he has never really watched The Great British Bake Off before. Worst of all, though, his description of Lawson is: “I remember my mum loved watching her growing up.” Being disorganised is one thing. Not watching Bake Off is one thing. But referring to Nigella Lawson in the past tense, as something only enjoyed by elderly people? This will not do.
Danni, 25, HGV service centre administrator, Dorset
![A young person holds up a yellow cake.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/dd55eb511dcc5c475b10a3e24b8ab53e5f73a84c/0_83_2372_2698/master/2372.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Danni sounds great, but I fear they are not long for the world. Describing their baking style as “Chaos, chaos, chaos!” (there’s that red flag again), they also describe their superpower as never giving up. “Even if I fail and fail and fail and fail, I just get back up and keep going and try again in a different way.” I don’t want to appear psychic here, guys, but I’m pretty sure Danni failed.
Gary, 67, retired garment technologist, Nottinghamshire
![An older man with grey hair holds up a cooling rack with cookies on it.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/49f5dcf673b31a5da99cee7dc2d99da0af0e7abc/0_169_2500_2956/master/2500.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Bake Off has been on the air for so long now that all its contestants tend to lapse into type. As such, Gary is this year’s “nice older man”. He’s pleasingly brief with his answers in the questionnaire, and appears to live very happily with his wife and all their animals. This is all good, of course, but expect him to be quickly outflanked by all the hungry youngsters who primarily see Bake off as a way to grow their Instagram followers.
Shannon, 29, project planner and scheduler, Gloucestershire
![A young woman with long, dark brown hair holds up a peace sign and pouts.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/8292fe4e8e8443b8bc65d19d82cdc5b8ad4b597f/0_118_2500_2836/master/2500.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Shannon is the exact opposite of Gary. By a wide margin, her questionnaire is the longest of the year, running to almost 2,000 words (for reference, Gary’s was about 500 words long). But what a wealth of information it is. For instance, we now know that she was a back-up baker on the show last year, that baking for the judges turned her stomach into “a swarm of butterflies” and that “Nigella brought this sensational presence into the tent, a kind of calm elegance that made the whole space feel homely and safe.” She seems lovely and earnest but – and I’m aware this is rich coming from me – the woman badly needs an editor.
Gabe, 32, artist and drag king, West Midlands
![A young man with tattoos and pierced ears holds up his hands and sticks his tongue out.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/4ab0e654249679f37efbe8a62f92c48971106fcf/0_0_2500_2793/master/2500.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
The “daddy of Birmingham drag”, Gabe describes themself as a “professional nuisance”. This may bear out. In their questionnaire, Gabe reveals that they did shots with Nigella, previously had their bum smacked by Alison Hammond and was ready to cream pie themselves in front of Noel Fielding. Every year I do these, without fail, I end up being followed on Instagram by one Bake Off contestant. I have a feeling that this year it’s going to be Gabe.
Moyin, 22, political economy student, Essex
![A young black man holds up a peace sign with one hand while holding a pink donut over one bespectacled eye with the other.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/9900500429e56359ba766d31e1058461b2c4dc28/0_0_2764_3235/master/2764.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
From what I can tell, Moyin likes to present as the high achiever of the group. He was an under-20 100m champion, could make macarons by the age of 14 and makes a point of noting that he often attends seminars on global political thought. Alas, his questionnaire has given him away, in that he gives a full-blown spoiler in it. I won’t repeat it, but it does involve Danni and genitalia. In other words, Moyin is a huge gossip and cannot be trusted.
Yannis, 28, paediatric doctor, London
![A dark-haired young man holds up a blue cake with red cherries on it.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/4009cf53032cfffcc3a19d6b4b3945b9b5de52c1/0_120_2797_3146/master/2797.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Yannis seems like a very composed, very thoughtful man. He is a Bangladeshi, born in Vienna but raised in London. He claims that Bake Off is the show that helped him learn to speak English. He puts great emphasis on caring for people. He is, as you will have seen, a paediatric doctor. So in that regard, I hope he does horribly here. The world needs more paediatric doctors and fewer people determined to leverage their stint on a cookery competition into semi-regular appearances on Sunday Brunch. Only instant failure can correct this cosmic unbalance.
Tom, 25, hairdresser, West Yorkshire
![A blond young man mixes blue batter in a bowl.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/8fae3f2893b8070cd2a70f11a841a13dc17503e5/0_212_2918_3436/master/2918.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Now we get to the bakers I think will actually do well. Based on his bio, Tom has the makings of a potential winner. He seems deeply unfazed by the prospect of appearing on Bake Off, not only because he describes himself as “super chill” but also because he seems to believe that it was his divine right to end up on the show. Also he claims to be obsessed by Nigella, which is the correct answer.
Nikki, 50, advertising post-producer, London
![A black woman with a fringe and patterned blouse coats a pastry with a wash.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/df9a092d9f4179945e05e5a16f467003cdd90849/63_124_2437_2891/master/2437.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
The primary thing to remember about Nikki is that she was once a podium dancer at Ziggy’s nightclub in Basingstoke in the 1990s. In truth, I am a little worried about Nikki, because in the questionnaire she described her baking style as “flavours, combinations and colours”, which is such a weirdly rudimentary statement that I’m worried she also describes her favourite film as “noises and shapes”. But, hey, anyone who danced on podiums in Basingstoke can almost certainly push through.
Connie, 63, NHS hospital discharge lead, London
![An older woman smiles and holds up a pastry.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/4a248243bedca1d241d61c1b45855aeb46b34a8a/80_140_2420_2827/master/2420.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Connie loves baking cakes so much that people literally call her “the Cake Lady”, and she isn’t upset by it. Plenty of the other bakers go out of their way to name Connie in their bios, too, which has to be a good sign of how well-liked she is. She also keeps a jar of fruit permanently soaking in rum, which is what poachers did in Danny the Champion of the World. What I’m trying to say is that Connie sounds like someone who could poach animals for a living, and I’m too terrified to put her lower on the list.
Molly, 31, accessibility coordinator, London
![A red headed woman coats a bake with some liquid.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/a4c2a25ad0bedbbb84db986c324fb80de38e8963/0_123_2500_3002/master/2500.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Molly has been baking since she was six. However, that isn’t why I think she will win Bake Off this year. No, I think she will win Bake Off because her bio states that she is 25% of the way through a 350,000-stitch cross-stitch landscape of Rivendell. Can you imagine the patience, the attention to detail, the sheer bloody-minded obsessiveness required to do such a thing? Clearly this is the woman to beat.
summary: Channel 4 has released the contestant biographies for the 2026 season of The Great British Bake Off, which is anticipated to be heavily focused on new judge Nigella Lawson. The article reviews the bakers and speculates on their chances of success based strictly on their official questionnaires. Contestants range from chaotic self-described novices to meticulous crafters poised to potentially win the competition.

Contestants include a wide variety of backgrounds, such as a paediatric doctor, a law student, a hairdresser, and a former podium dancer.
Several bakers, like Clara, Mo, and Danni, display traits described as chaotic red flags in their questionnaires.

title: Oasis recordings up for auction despite band’s objections
author: Nadia Khomami
content:
An archive of more than 100 hours of Oasis recordings, including concerts, rehearsals and candid conversations between Noel and Liam Gallagher, is to be auctioned for up to £1.6m despite objections from the band.
The collection was amassed by the band’s sound engineer Huw Richards, who worked with Oasis from the release of their 1994 debut album, Definitely Maybe, until 2001. It comprises 209 DAT tapes, 73 analogue cassettes and three MiniDiscs, and is being sold by Richards’s son, Owain.
Littleton Auctions in Evesham, Worcestershire, has given the archive a guide price of between £1.2m and £1.6m, with the sale due to take place on 3 October.
Ben Homer, the auction house’s managing director, said Oasis had expressed concerns about the sale.
![Liam and Noel Gallagher in 1996. Liam sits at the front of the stage wearing a black hoodie and laughing, holding a can of lager, while Noel stands behind him with his arms held up and outstretched.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/7809658acb993acfb1397dc2fff1f6d559577e4c/0_0_2532_3792/master/2532.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
“The Oasis camp is aware of the auction and has expressed concerns, which is entirely understandable given the scale and significance of the material,” he said in a statement to the Guardian.
Homer said the auction house was handling the sale through the appropriate legal process and the recordings were being offered with verified provenance. He said the archive would give collectors and institutions the opportunity to acquire material documenting an important period in British music.
The collection includes what is believed to be the only recording of Oasis’s 1996 concert on the banks of Loch Lomond in Scotland. It also contains recordings of numerous rehearsals and soundchecks, as well as informal conversations involving the Gallagher brothers and members of the touring crew.
Owain Richards, who is also a sound engineer, said he had previously been in discussions with Oasis’s management after the band sought some of the recordings.
He told the Times those discussions had ultimately “fizzled away” and that the band wanted the tapes returned rather than sold elsewhere.
Richards said his father had meticulously preserved the recordings, which date from a period when concertgoers were far less likely to make their own recordings on mobile phones. “It really is a piece of history,” he said.
Richards said the audio remained in sufficiently good condition to be mastered for a live album. The recordings cannot, however, simply be released by whoever buys them. Oasis retain the intellectual property rights, meaning the archive cannot be commercially exploited without the band’s cooperation.
after newsletter promotion
Littleton Auctions has described the collection as a significant record of the band’s live career and said it could be of interest to collectors, scholars and museums.
The auction comes as interest in Oasis continues to grow since the band’s reunion last year, when Noel and Liam Gallagher returned to the stage together for the first time in 15 years.
Oasis became one of the biggest British rock bands of the 1990s, with albums including (What’s the Story) Morning Glory? and Be Here Now. Their career was marked by the fractious relationship between the Gallagher brothers, whose arguments eventually contributed to the band’s split in 2009.
The reunion saw Oasis play sold-out dates in Britain, North America, Australia and Asia. The brothers were also pictured together at the Venice film festival this weekend, where Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger, a film documenting their return, was premiered.
The Littleton auction will also feature other Oasis memorabilia, including a pair of Adidas Kegler Super Ostrich trainers given to Noel Gallagher. Oasis were approached for comment.
summary: An archive of over 100 hours of Oasis recordings, amassed by former sound engineer Huw Richards, is set to be auctioned for up to £1.6m despite objections from the band. The collection features concerts, rehearsals, and candid conversations between Noel and Liam Gallagher from 1994 to 2001. While the buyer will own the physical tapes, Oasis retains the intellectual property rights, meaning the recordings cannot be commercially released without the band's cooperation.
key_points: An archive of more than 100 hours of Oasis recordings is scheduled to be auctioned by Littleton Auctions on 3 October.
The collection was gathered by the band's former sound engineer Huw Richards and is being sold by his son, Owain.
The guide price for the archive, which includes DAT tapes, analogue cassettes, and MiniDiscs, is between £1.2m and £1.6m.
Oasis has expressed concerns about the sale and previously sought the return of the tapes.
The buyer cannot commercially exploit the recordings because Oasis retains the intellectual property rights.

title: New Inbetweeners film confirmed by Netflix as lead stars return
author: Naomi de Souza
content:
![Simon Bird, Joe Thomas, James Buckley and Blake Harrison pose for photos at the world premiere of The Inbetweeners 2. The group are all wearing suits with skinny ties.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/de56/live/c2d84b40-aa95-11f1-ab09-7f2415c9a652.jpg)
Netflix has confirmed the lead stars of the coming-of-age sitcom are set to reprise their roles for The Inbetweeners 3
- Published
Ooh, sequel friend! A new Inbetweeners movie is officially in the works, Netflix has confirmed.
The original cast of Simon Bird, James Buckley, Blake Harrison and Joe Thomas will reprise their roles for the feature film, with production starting on Monday.
The Inbetweeners 3 will follow on the story of their characters, Will McKenzie, Jay Cartwright, Neil Sutherland and Simon Cooper.
They originally starred in three seasons of the popular coming-of-age sitcom, which aired on E4 between 2008 and 2010.
It followed their trials and misadventures as suburban teenagers at the fictional Rudge Park Comprehensive.
The show has gained new fans over the years due to some of its best bits finding new life on social media, as well as through the film sequels.
The third instalment follows two sequels backed by Film4, which were released in 2011 and 2014.
Alongside the announcement, Netflix released a teaser video which showed Will, Simon, Neil and Jay return to their iconic yellow Fiat.
The friend group all get into the tiny car but Simon struggles to start the engine.
After some encouragement, it gets going and they drive out of what looks like a storage unit.
![James Buckley, Blake Harrison, Joe Thomas and Simon Bird pose at a premier of The Inbetweeners 2 in front of a billboard of the film. James wears a grey waterproof, Blake blue and white patterned top, Joe wears a grey blazer over a navy shirt and Simon wears checked patterned shirt.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/06d6/live/44806ec0-aa96-11f1-ab09-7f2415c9a652.jpg)
The third instalment follows two Film4 backed sequels, which were released in 2011 and 2014
Production kicks off after months of speculation that there would be another film, but beyond the lead characters returning, the rest of the cast is yet to be confirmed.
Fans will be wondering if English actress Emily Atack will return in her role as Charlotte Hinchcliffe, or if Emily Head will come back as Carli D'Amato.
However, Netflix has announced The Inbetweeners creators, Damon Beesley and Iain Morris, will return to write and direct the film.
Beesley and Morris said it has been "super fun" hanging out with friends again.
"We're going to work hard every week to ensure there are no problemos making this new film for humans," they added.
![A footer logo for BBC Newsbeat. It has the BBC logo and the word Newsbeat in white over a colorful background of violet, purple and orange shapes. At the bottom a black square reading "Listen on Sounds" is visible.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/976/cpsprodpb/e185/live/c8857230-14f0-11ef-976f-87c9f89e656e.jpg)
summary: Netflix has officially confirmed that a third Inbetweeners film is in development, with production set to begin on Monday. Original cast members Simon Bird, James Buckley, Blake Harrison, and Joe Thomas will all reprise their starring roles. The new feature follows two previous film sequels released in 2011 and 2014, with creators Damon Beesley and Iain Morris returning to write and direct.
key_points: Netflix has confirmed a new Inbetweeners film is officially in production.
Original lead stars Simon Bird, James Buckley, Blake Harrison, and Joe Thomas are returning to their roles.
Creators Damon Beesley and Iain Morris will write and direct the upcoming third installment.
A teaser released by Netflix shows the characters returning to their iconic yellow Fiat.

title: Cruz Beckham appears to take another swipe at brother Brooklyn following Nicola Peltz’s Venice appearance
author: Joe Harker
content:
![Cruz Beckham appears to take another swipe at brother Brooklyn following Nicola Peltz’s Venice appearance](https://resizer.ladbiblegroup.com/unsafe/rs:fit:3840:0:0:0/g:sm/q:70/aHR0cHM6Ly9ldS1pbWFnZXMuY29udGVudHN0YWNrLmNvbS92My9hc3NldHMvYmx0Y2Q3NGFjYzFkMGE5OWYzYS9ibHRkOGRkMGMxNDgyMjFjZTc3LzZhOWQ4YTY5NzEwY2M4ZmY5OTIxMjBjOS9icm9va2x5bi5wbmc.webp)
Cruz Beckham has made another post some have interpreted as a hit out at his older brother Brooklyn.
The feud between the Beckhams has been evident for some time now as Brooklyn has accused his parents David and Victoria of trying to control his life, 'ruin' his relationship with his wife and put their brand above him.
He even made reference to it in an advert for the 2026 World Cup where he joked about a 'long story' being the reason he was watching it at home, having said he 'does not want to reconcile'.
One of Brooklyn's fiercer critics among the ranks of the Beckham family is his brother Cruz, who has accused Brooklyn of making things up and firmly sided with his parents in the feud.
Advert
Yesterday he posted a family photo with the love heart emoji and since there was one very notable absence it's been interpreted as a swipe at Brooklyn by some fans.
Perhaps it is, but given they're not on speaking terms if Cruz Beckham wants to post a family photo then it's going to have to be without Brooklyn.
Some of his followers decided they didn't want him to feel left out and tagged him in the post comments, though others suggested Cruz had 'posted this after photos appeared of Brooklyn & Nicola in Venice'.
![If Cruz Beckham wants to post a family photo he can't do it with Brooklyn in now (Jeff Spicer/Getty Images for YSL Beauty)](https://resizer.ladbiblegroup.com/unsafe/rs:fit:3840:0:0:0/g:sm/q:70/aHR0cHM6Ly9ldS1pbWFnZXMuY29udGVudHN0YWNrLmNvbS92My9hc3NldHMvYmx0Y2Q3NGFjYzFkMGE5OWYzYS9ibHRkODA3MGZjNjNkOTI3ZDQ5LzZhOWQ4Yjg0YTIwYTIwYzBjNmQ3ODYxYy9jcnUuanBn.webp)
Brooklyn and his wife Nicola Peltz were pictured at the Venice Film Festival, leading some to wonder if Cruz was posting his happy family picture in response to that.
Others just quipped 'some people don't know what they're missing'.
![Brooklyn and Nicola were in Venice for the film festival (Benjamin Cremel/Getty Images)](https://resizer.ladbiblegroup.com/unsafe/rs:fit:3840:0:0:0/g:sm/q:70/aHR0cHM6Ly9ldS1pbWFnZXMuY29udGVudHN0YWNrLmNvbS92My9hc3NldHMvYmx0Y2Q3NGFjYzFkMGE5OWYzYS9ibHQzNTFkYzk2YmZjMjA0MjZkLzZhOWQ4YTA3NjFmZDczNDVhNTNmMjliNi9icm9va2x5bi1uaWNvbGEuanBn.webp)
Timeline of the Beckham family feud
April 2022: Brooklyn and Nicola tie the knot
On 9 April 2022, Brooklyn and Nicola got married in a lavish ceremony in front of 500 guests at her family's estate in Palm Beach, Florida, two years after getting engaged.
Aug 2022: The first reports of a feud between Nicola and Victoria Beckham
Just months after the wedding, media sources were starting to report on a 'full-on cold war' between Nicola and her new mum-in-law.
According to Page Six, 'the build-up to the wedding was horrendous' and they 'can’t stand each other and don’t talk'.
Reports also claimed much of the feud came from Nicola's decision to wear a Valentino wedding dress instead of a piece designed by Victoria's fashion house, but they appeared to quash these rumours.
March 2023: The Beckhams play happy families
In March 2023, the Beckhams seemed to be happier than ever and were posing for photos at Victoria's Paris fashion show.
April 2025: The family rift resurfaces
Two years on, it was reported that Brooklyn and Nicola had snubbed David's 50th birthday party at Cipriani Downtown Miami.
And then, just days later, TMZ claimed that Brooklyn and brother Romeo weren't speaking due to a fallout over Romeo's girlfriend, Kim Turnbull, who had a 'romantic connection' with Brooklyn 'several years ago'.
Cruz later insisted that Brooklyn and Kim had never actually dated, and in May of 2025, Brooklyn and Nicola were nowhere to be seen as the birthday celebrations for David continued.
July 2025: Mass unfollowing on social media
In July 2025, Brooklyn and Nicola unfollowed Romeo and Cruz and vice versa.
August 2025: David and Victoria miss vow renewals
The following month, David and Victoria are reported not to have attended the Peltz-Beckham vow renewals.
And by December that year, it was reported that Brooklyn no longer followed his parents, and they no longer followed him, and the youngest brother was quick to set the record straight.
Dec 2025: Cruz speaks out
Cruz wrote on his Instagram Stories about the claims that he and his family had unfollowed Brooklyn: "NOT TRUE. My mum and dad would never unfollow their son … Let's get the facts right. They woke up blocked … as did I."
Jan 2026: Brooklyn takes legal action
In January 2026, it was claimed that Brooklyn sent a legal letter to his parents, insisting they only contact him via his lawyer; a rule which Victoria is believed to have broken when she 'liked' an Instagram post he made about a roast chicken.
Jan 2026: Brooklyn breaks silence on family feud
In a shock statement posted on his Instagram Stories on 19 January, Brooklyn made some bombshell claims about his family, which included how his parents have tried to 'ruin' his relationship with Nicola, have always 'controlled' his life, and how 'Brand Beckham' comes first before anything else.
March 2026: David reaches out to Brooklyn
David shared a post to celebrate Brooklyn’s birthday, writing: "27 Today. Happy Birthday Bust. We love you."
He shared an old photo of Brooklyn as a child and tagged Victoria, but was unable to tag Brooklyn since his son has blocked him.
The post was met with stony silence from Brooklyn.
June 2026: Harper turns up at Brooklyn’s door
Harper, Brooklyn’s 14-year-old sister and the Beckhams’ youngest child, was photographed outside Brooklyn’s door hand-delivering a letter. Brooklyn and Nicola were believed to be in New York at the time.
A rep for the Peltz-Beckhams savagely responded: "That photographers were in place as the letter was hand-delivered says it all - this was choreographed for the cameras."
Meanwhile, Brooklyn releases a DoorDash World Cup ad clearly taking a swipe at his family. He says in the commercial: “You’re probably wondering why I’m watching the FIFA World Cup 2026 from home. It’s a long story."
Topics: Brooklyn Beckham, Nicola Peltz, Celebrity
summary: Cruz Beckham shared a family photo on social media accompanied by a heart emoji, which fans interpreted as a swipe at his estranged brother, Brooklyn. The post followed public appearances by Brooklyn and his wife, Nicola Peltz, at the Venice Film Festival. The ongoing Beckham family feud has involved public statements, social media blocks, and strained relations between Brooklyn and his parents.
key_points: Cruz Beckham posted a family photo that notably excluded his brother Brooklyn, prompting speculation from fans.
The timing of Cruz's post coincided with photos of Brooklyn and Nicola Peltz appearing at the Venice Film Festival.
Brooklyn has previously accused his parents, David and Victoria, of controlling his life and prioritizing their brand.
The ongoing family rift features mutual social media blocking, public statements, and a lack of communication between Brooklyn and the rest of the family.

title: Casualty confirms when show will return after 40th anniversary episodes
author: Stephanie Chase
content:
Casualty has confirmed when it will be back on our screens following its 40th anniversary double bill. The soap celebrated four decades on the BBC on Saturday (September 5) with a two-episode special which featured a major explosion. 
During the end credits of the episode, BBC One's continuity announcer told viewers: "For 40 years, Casualty has been the beating heart of our Saturday nights.
"The best is yet to come, with some exciting changes ahead. Don't miss the new era of Casualty, coming next year to BBC One and iPlayer."
Related: Best streaming services
We already know that Casualty is set to move from Holby to a fictional Welsh hospital, with the BBC announcing the big change last year as it looked for a new producer.
A statement from the BBC read: "We are asking tenderers to include authentic representation of Wales and reflect the reality of the Welsh NHS.
"This is not about radical change of the show, although the move to Welsh portrayal will mean a new fictional hospital based in Wales, and tenderers will need to address this core change in their editorial pitch to the evaluation panel.
"The successful tenderer will need to be able to demonstrate how to incorporate Welsh portrayal and maintain familiarity at the same time."
Casualty's 40th anniversary episode saw Kellie Shirley making her return as Sophia Peters, only to die from injuries suffered in the St James’ Hospital has exploded, leading to her ex Dylan (Will Beck) suffering a disturbing breakdown.
The episode also saw the returns of Charlie Fairhead (Derek Thompson) and Ethan Hardy ( (George Rainsford).
Related: How Casualty's sensational anniversary episodes set up the show's new era
Last year, Milo Clarke, who plays Teddy Gowan, spoke about the show's move to Wales, assuring fans that the soap will only get better.
"We film in Wales, so Wales feels like our home anyway," Clarke told Digital Spy exclusively.
"The fans might have to adjust a little bit, but hopefully we take across everything that we know and love about the show. And we’ll be in a good place, we’ll be in a great place, we’ll be in a stronger place – and we’re going to come back fighting. It’ll be great."
Casualty airs on Saturday nights on BBC One and now streams first on BBC iPlayer, where episodes are released at 6am on the day of transmission.

Following this milestone, the show will return for a new era next year on BBC One and iPlayer. As part of this upcoming transition, the series is moving from Holby to a new fictional hospital based in Wales.

The anniversary episodes featured a major hospital explosion and the returns of characters including Sophia Peters, Charlie Fairhead, and Ethan Hardy.

title: Kim Kardashian, Kanye West Step Out to Support North West at First Headlining Show

Kim Kardashian and Kanye “Ye” West are keeping up with their kids’ passions.
The SKIMS founder and Grammy winner each stepped out to cheer on their daughter North West as she performed at her first headline concert at The Vic Theatre in Chicago, Illinois, Sept. 5.
In footage shared online, Kim and Kanye—who also share kids Saint West, 10, Chicago West, 8, and Psalm West, 7—could be seen arriving separately to the event, with The Kardashians star donning a slicked back ponytail as she took her seat in the VIP section.
Meanwhile, Kanye arrived later donning a brown bomber jacket and sunglasses as he filmed his daughter onstage.
Kim, for her part, shared her own memories from the unforgettable evening. In one video shared to Instagram Stories, Kim captured the screaming crowd waving at her from her perched section.
In another post, Kim shared a snap of a fan holding up a sign that read, “We’re from the North West side.”
North, 13, released her debut EP N0rth4evr in May, telling Dazed in August that she finds performing the material "fun, relieving and exciting."
As for what pushed the teen to pursue her music dreams now?
Well, North shared the worst advice she’s ever received is “to start my career later.”
"It’s like, nah, this is my hobby,” she explained, "this is what I like to do, this is what I wanna do with my life.”
North's concert marked a rare joint sighting for her parents, who divorced in 2022 after nearly eight years of marriage.
Previously, Kim shared insight into the breakup’s affect on her family.
"When you have kids, it’s definitely harder to leave than it is to stay,” Kim said on an October 2025 episode of Call Her Daddy. “And it changes everyone’s life forever.”
Though Kim and Kanye ended up going their separate ways, the reality star has made peace with the decision, noting, "an over-a-decade relationship with four beautiful children is not a failure.”
Though Kim shared it's "not easy" coparenting with Kanye, she’s dedicated to making it work for the sake of their little ones.
“I had the best dad,” she told Angie Martinez on her IRL Podcast in 2022. “I have the best memories and the greatest experience. And that’s all I want for my kids. As long as they can have that, that’s what I would want for them.”

content:

title: Susan Sarandon Says She Is Still Losing Hollywood Roles Due To Palestine-Israel Stance
author: Melanie Goodfellow; Nada Aboul Kheir
content:
![](https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/GettyImages-2293795997.jpg?w=681&h=383&crop=1) 
Susan Sarandon told a press conference in Venice on Sunday that she continued to lose big roles due to her public support of Palestine, even if the narrative around the nature of U.S. support of Israel has changed in recent months.
“I’ve still had movies taken away recently because there are agencies that are telling people not to hire me still. But that’s the power structure. I think within the people, certainly internationally, I feel welcome,” she said in response to a question from Deadline.
“So it depends. If it’s a major studio, I think there is, not just with me but with other people, that have been told that that is impossible in terms of being able to do this film.”
The Oscar-winning actress was speaking at the Venice Film Festival press conference for Andrea Pallaoro’s Golden Lion contender The Echo Chamber, an adaptation of Bernardo Bertolucci’s final screenplay.
Watch on Deadline
She stars as storied songstress Ava who engages engages a music producer (Luca Marinelli) with a history of drug addiction to work on her comeback album, becoming the third wheel in his complex relationship with a physiotherapist (Alicia Vikander), who is her antithesis in her private, quiet approach to life.
“I thank Andrea for that because he didn’t listen to the warnings,” she continued. “So I think yes, there has been a change in terms of understanding of the situation, and I think the general public. But there are still very strongly held positions within my industry that are held by Zionists and who have not relaxed their feelings towards me, but I found my family, I found my people, and I’m okay.”
The Thelma And Louise star, who was dropped by UTA in 2023 after attending several rallies in support of Palestine and making an inflammatory comment, has revealed in the past that roles dried up for as a result of her activism.
Her comments come amid a continuing stand-off in Hollywood over the Middle East conflict after Paramount accused Mark Ruffalo of using “antisemitic tropes” in a post criticizing the Paramount-WBD merger, in which he raised concerns over its backer Oracle‘s involvement in supplying technology amid the Israel-Hamas conflict.
The conflict has also become a hot button topic at Venice, with activists calling on the festival to raise the Palestinian flag in recognition of the Palestinian directors in selection. Festival Artistic Director Alberto Barbera has said this is not possible due to the fact Palestine is not officially recognized as a state by Italy.
Earlier in the press conference, Sarandon said that she felt the wider narrative about Palestine and Israel had shifted in the U.S.
“I think that the narrative has completely changed in terms of the historical relevance of Palestine and the ties of Zionists with America and our politics, that has been a major revelation for people,” she said.
“How much money the United States gives to Israel? Nobody really understood that. And also, now we have voted to combine the army of the United States with the army of Israel. So there’s a lot of things that people are aware of now,” she said
Her comments on the combining of the U.S. army with that of Israel were in reference to the U.S. House of Representatives’ approval of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) on July 22, Section 219 of which controversially expands U.S.-Israel defense technology cooperation.
Critics claims it effectively merges the U.S. and Israeli militaries, while supporters say that is categorically not the case and that it rather strengthens a longstanding strategic partnership.
summary: Oscar-winning actress Susan Sarandon stated at a Venice Film Festival press conference that she continues to lose major Hollywood roles and faces boycotts from agencies due to her public support for Palestine. Sarandon was dropped by UTA in 2023 following her participation in pro-Palestinian rallies, though she expressed gratitude to director Andrea Pallaoro for casting her in 'The Echo Chamber' despite industry warnings. She also noted that while the general public's awareness and narrative surrounding the Israel-Palestine conflict have shifted, strong opposition persists within the entertainment industry.
key_points: Susan Sarandon stated she continues to lose film roles because agencies instruct people not to hire her due to her Palestine stance.
Sarandon previously lost representation with UTA in 2023 after attending pro-Palestinian rallies and making inflammatory comments.
She thanked director Andrea Pallaoro for casting her in 'The Echo Chamber' despite industry warnings.
Sarandon believes the general public's narrative and understanding of the Israel-Palestine conflict have significantly shifted.

title: Former Every Time I Die guitarist and AEW wrestler Andy Williams dead at 48
author: Merlin Alderslade
content:
![Andy Williams playing guitar](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/TE5LQmPGCDoAmgg8nj4Q4E.jpg) 
Andy Williams, former guitarist of New York metalcore innovators Every Time I Die and professional wrestler, has died aged 48, it has been reported. Williams collapsed while performing in a wrestling match at an event in Pennsylvania yesterday, Saturday September 5, according to TMZ. No official cause of death has been confirmed.
A founding member of Every Time I Die upon the band's formation in Buffalo, New York in 1998, Williams and his bandmates would emerge as one of the most influential forces in 21st century metalcore. Williams served as the the band's rhythm guitarist throughout their entire time together right up until their surprising implosion in 2022.
Every Time I Die produced nine studio albums, the most recent of which, Radical, was released in 2021 to critical acclaim.
Williams was also a longtime professional wrestling fan and harboured ambitions of becoming a wrestler himself. He realised that dream after making his professional debut on the independent wrestling circuit in 2015, taking on the moniker of 'The Butcher' and forming a tag team with Jesse 'The Blade' Guilmette. The duo would receive international recognition upon appearances with powerhouse company All Elite Wrestling from 2019 onwards.
In a 2022 interview, Williams compared his career in music with his wrestling endeavours, telling Reneé Paquette's podcast: "I don't know how to read music. I just picked up a guitar and it just made sense. To me, it was more like Tetris than anything. I would just make these shapes up in my head and I would play these shapes.
"If I wrote out music, it would only make sense to me and the dudes I was in the band with. A lot of it is like X's and O's, or I'll use squares for certain things and triangles for certain things. It really turned into more of, like, a video game to me than making music."
"Wrestling, to me, is like writing a song," he added. "Once I kind of understood how to write that 'song', it was like, 'Oh, ok, that's cool - there's an intro, there's an outro, there's a chorus.' It really does work like that."
